# bestax

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma)
[![create-bestax](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/create-bestax.svg?label=create-bestax)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/create-bestax)
[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-100%25-blue.svg)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
[![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-99%25-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/allxsmith/bestax/blob/main/bulma-ui/vitest.config.ts)
[![Bulma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bulma-v1.0+-00d1b2.svg)](https://bulma.io)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Socket Badge](https://badge.socket.dev/npm/package/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/latest)](https://socket.dev/npm/package/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/overview)
[![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/allxsmith/bestax/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/allxsmith/bestax)
[![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14361/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14361)
[![npm provenance](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-provenance-3fb950.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma#provenance)
[![Security policy](https://img.shields.io/badge/security-policy-blue.svg)](https://github.com/allxsmith/bestax/blob/main/SECURITY.md)

TypeScript-first React component library for the **Bulma v1** CSS framework — 110+ fully typed components — plus a project scaffolder and AI agent tooling.

## 📋 At a glance

|                      |                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Library**          | [`@allxsmith/bestax-bulma`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma) — `npm install @allxsmith/bestax-bulma`                                                     |
| **Scaffolder**       | [`create-bestax`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/create-bestax) — `npm create bestax@latest my-app`                                                                             |
| **Requires**         | React `^18 \|\| ^19` (+ `react-dom`). Bulma v1 is the library's only runtime dependency — installed automatically                                                              |
| **Styles**           | `import '@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/bestax.css';` — Bulma v1 + the bestax extras ([more flavors](#-styling-and-theming))                                                          |
| **Icons (optional)** | Font Awesome, Material Design Icons, Ionicons, Material Icons, Material Symbols — all optional peer dependencies                                                               |
| **Docs**             | [bestax.io](https://bestax.io) · [Storybook](https://bestax.io/storybook)                                                                                                      |
| **LLM docs**         | [llms.txt](https://bestax.io/llms.txt) (curated index) · [llms-full.txt](https://bestax.io/llms-full.txt) (complete docs, one file)                                            |
| **Agent Skills**     | `npx skills add https://github.com/allxsmith/bestax --skill bestax-layout-scaffold` ([the full roster](skills/README.md))                                                      |
| **Community**        | [Discord](https://discord.gg/zehJrQGtKu) · [dev.to](https://dev.to/allxsmith) · [Medium](https://medium.com/@allxsmith) · [Issues](https://github.com/allxsmith/bestax/issues) |

> **If you are an AI agent or LLM:** fetch **<https://bestax.io/llms.txt>** for a curated index of the full documentation, or **<https://bestax.io/llms-full.txt>** for the complete docs in a single file, before answering questions about or writing code with this library. Every page on [bestax.io](https://bestax.io) is also available as raw markdown — see the [LLMs guide](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/llms).

**Full documentation, guides, and API reference: 👉 [https://bestax.io](https://bestax.io)** — the docs site is always the most complete and up-to-date resource.

---

## 🚀 Quick start

### New project

Scaffold a Vite app with everything wired up (CSS flavor, icon library, optional AI skills + `CLAUDE.md`):

```bash
npm create bestax@latest my-app
# or: pnpm create bestax my-app
```

Useful flags: `-t vite|vite-ts` (template), `-b complete|prefixed|no-helpers|no-helpers-prefixed|no-dark-mode` (CSS flavor), `-i fontawesome|mdi|ionicons|material-icons|material-symbols|none` (icons), `--skills` (install the [Agent Skills](#-for-ai-tools) into `.claude/skills`), `-y` (accept defaults). See the [create-bestax README](create-bestax/README.md).

### Existing project

```bash
npm install @allxsmith/bestax-bulma
# or: pnpm add @allxsmith/bestax-bulma
```

Import the bundled CSS once (Bulma v1 + the bestax extras), then use components:

```tsx
import '@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/bestax.css';
import { Button } from '@allxsmith/bestax-bulma';

function App() {
  return (
    <Button color="primary" onClick={() => alert('Clicked!')}>
      Click Me
    </Button>
  );
}
```

Prefer stock Bulma? `import 'bulma/css/bulma.min.css';` works too — you'll just miss the bestax-only components' styles (add `@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/extras.css` for those).

Theming, dark mode, and configuration are one wrapper away:

```tsx
import { Theme, ConfigProvider } from '@allxsmith/bestax-bulma';

function Root() {
  return (
    <Theme isRoot colorMode="system">
      {/* colorMode: 'light' | 'dark' | 'system' */}
      <ConfigProvider iconLibrary="fa">
        <App />
      </ConfigProvider>
    </Theme>
  );
}
```

[Installation guide](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/getting-started/installation) · [Configuration](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/features/configuration)

---

## 📦 What's in this repo

| Path                                 | Package                                                                                            | What it is                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`bulma-ui/`](bulma-ui/)             | [`@allxsmith/bestax-bulma`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@allxsmith/bestax-bulma)                 | The component library                                                                                     |
| [`create-bestax/`](create-bestax/)   | [`create-bestax`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/create-bestax)                                     | Project scaffolder — `npm create bestax@latest`                                                           |
| [`bestax-migrate/`](bestax-migrate/) | [`bestax-migrate`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bestax-migrate)                                   | Codemods for migrating existing apps from other React Bulma libraries                                     |
| [`bestax-mcp/`](bestax-mcp/)         | [`bestax-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bestax-mcp)                                           | MCP server — component props, examples and skills for AI coding agents                                    |
| [`eslint-plugin/`](eslint-plugin/)   | [`@allxsmith/eslint-plugin-bestax`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@allxsmith/eslint-plugin-bestax) | ESLint rules — catches helper-prop values the library silently drops                                      |
| [`docs/`](docs/)                     | —                                                                                                  | Docusaurus source of [bestax.io](https://bestax.io)                                                       |
| [`skills/`](skills/)                 | —                                                                                                  | [Agent Skills](https://bestax.io/docs/skills/intro) for coding agents (also bundled into `create-bestax`) |

The published packages are versioned and released independently.

---

## 🧩 Components

110+ components covering all of Bulma v1, plus bestax extras (Carousel, Dialog, Sidebar, Steps, date/time pickers, and more):

- **[Elements](https://bestax.io/docs/api/elements/button)** — Button, Table, Tag, Title, Icon, Image, Notification, Progress, Skeleton, Content, Delete, and typed HTML wrappers (Paragraph, Span, Figure, lists, …)
- **[Components](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/modal)** — Navbar, Modal, Card, Dropdown, Menu, Message, Pagination, Panel, Tabs, Breadcrumb, Toast, Tooltip, Steps, Sidebar, Carousel, Collapse, Dialog, Loading
- **[Form](https://bestax.io/docs/api/form/input)** — Field/Control, Input, Select, TextArea, Checkbox(es), Radio(s), Switch, Slider, Rate, File, Numberinput, Autocomplete, Taginput, and DateInput / TimeInput / DateTimeInput pickers
- **[Layout](https://bestax.io/docs/api/layout/container)** — Container, Section, Hero, Level, Media, Footer
- **[Columns](https://bestax.io/docs/api/columns)** & **[Grid](https://bestax.io/docs/api/grid)** — classic 12-column flexbox columns and the Bulma v1 CSS Grid
- **[Helpers](https://bestax.io/docs/api/helpers/theme)** — `Theme`, `ConfigProvider`, `useBulmaClasses`, `classNames`

> Migrating from v2? Snackbar was merged into [Toast](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/toast) in v3 — see the [migration guides](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/getting-started/migration).

---

## 🎨 Styling and theming

Pick one CSS flavor (all shipped with the library — matching `create-bestax -b`):

| Import                                                            | What you get                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/bestax.css`                              | **Default.** Bulma v1 + bestax extras                                               |
| `@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/versions/bestax-prefixed.css`            | All classes prefixed `bestax-` — pair with `<ConfigProvider classPrefix="bestax-">` |
| `@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/versions/bestax-no-helpers.css`          | Without Bulma helper classes                                                        |
| `@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/versions/bestax-no-helpers-prefixed.css` | Prefixed, without helpers                                                           |
| `@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/versions/bestax-no-dark-mode.css`        | Without dark-mode styles                                                            |
| `@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/extras.css`                              | bestax extras only — for use alongside stock `bulma/css/bulma.min.css`              |
| `@allxsmith/bestax-bulma/scss/*`                                  | Raw SCSS for full customization                                                     |

- **Dark mode:** `<Theme colorMode="dark">` (or `"system"` to follow the OS) — [docs](https://bestax.io/docs/api/helpers/theme)
- **Brand colors, fonts, radius:** the [`Theme`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/helpers/theme) component overrides Bulma's `--bulma-*` CSS variables (globally with `isRoot`, or scoped to a subtree). Default primary color is `#1e6b99`
- **Class prefixing & icon defaults:** [`ConfigProvider`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/helpers/config) sets `classPrefix` and `iconLibrary` for a whole tree
- **CSS variables reference:** [docs](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/features/css-variables)

---

## 🤖 For AI Tools

Building with an AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot)? bestax-bulma ships LLM-optimized docs:

- 📘 **[LLMs guide](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/llms)** — how to use the library with AI tools
- 📄 **[llms.txt](https://bestax.io/llms.txt)** — curated index · **[llms-full.txt](https://bestax.io/llms-full.txt)** — the full docs in one file · every docs page is also served as raw markdown
- 🔌 **[MCP server](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/llms#mcp-server)** — let the agent _query_ the library instead of reading it: props (including compound parts), ~900 examples, `--bulma-*` variables, and the skills as prompts. Offline, and pinned to the version you have installed.

  ```bash
  claude mcp add bestax -- npx -y bestax-mcp
  ```

- 🧩 **[Agent Skills](https://bestax.io/docs/skills/intro)** — teach your agent the bestax way:

  | Skill                     | Use it when…                                                                     |
  | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `bestax-layout-scaffold`  | Turning a high-level request (dashboard, landing page, …) into a responsive page |
  | `bestax-form`             | Building forms — Field/Control composition and the full input inventory          |
  | `bestax-theming`          | Customizing colors, fonts, dark mode via `Theme` and `--bulma-*` variables       |
  | `bestax-custom-component` | Building a new custom component beyond stock Bulma, the bestax way               |
  | `bestax-icons`            | Adding icons — Icon/IconText and the five supported icon libraries               |
  | `bestax-optimize`         | Shrinking the built CSS — flavor builds, modular Sass, import hygiene            |
  | `bestax-migrate`          | Moving an app off react-bulma-components, rbx, bloomer or raw Bulma classes      |

  ```bash
  npx skills add https://github.com/allxsmith/bestax --skill bestax-layout-scaffold
  ```

  New projects get the skills automatically with `npm create bestax@latest my-app --skills` (plus a generated `CLAUDE.md`).

- 🧰 **[bestax plugin](https://github.com/allxsmith/bestax-skills)**: the skills and the MCP server in one install. In Claude Code:

  ```text
  /plugin marketplace add allxsmith/bestax-skills
  /plugin install bestax@bestax
  ```

  [Other agents](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/llms#bestax-plugin) install it from the same repository.

---

## ⭐ Why bestax-bulma?

- **Built for Bulma v1.x** — most other React Bulma libraries are stuck on Bulma 0.9.4
- **100% TypeScript** — every component and prop fully typed
- **One runtime dependency: Bulma** — it ships with the library; clean install, fewer security concerns
- **Tree-shakeable** — import what you need and ship only that: unused components drop out of the ESM build, and modular Sass does the same for CSS. A CJS build covers `require`
- **99% test coverage** — enforced in CI by the [Vitest config](bulma-ui/vitest.config.ts), not just claimed
- **Active developer support** — issues, questions, and PRs get fast responses

---

## 🔒 Hardened by default

Supply-chain security here is a standing constraint on how the project is built, not a checklist we filled in once:

- **Signed provenance on every release** — each tarball carries a sigstore attestation linking it to the exact commit and CI run that produced it. Check it yourself with `npm audit signatures`, or on the package page's Provenance section.
- **npm OIDC trusted publishing** — releases authenticate with short-lived, per-run tokens. There is no long-lived `NPM_TOKEN` in this repo to steal.
- **Signed release commits** — release commits and tags are GPG-signed, and `main` rejects unsigned commits outright.
- **Socket.dev scans every PR** — dependency changes are checked for malware, install scripts, obfuscated code, and privilege escalation before they can reach `main`.
- **Every GitHub Action pinned to a full commit SHA** — no movable tags, so a compromised action release can't roll silently into the pipeline.
- **Install scripts blocked by default** — dependency `install`/`postinstall` scripts don't run unless explicitly allow-listed one at a time, each with a written rationale ([`pnpm-workspace.yaml`](pnpm-workspace.yaml)).
- **3-day dependency cooldown** — freshly published versions won't install. This is the main defense against account-takeover worms, which are usually yanked within hours.
- **Frozen lockfile + audit gate** — CI installs exactly what the reviewed lockfile resolves and fails on high-severity advisories.
- **CodeQL, Dependency Review, and Dependabot** — static analysis over both the source and the workflow files, PR-level advisory blocking, and weekly grouped dependency updates.
- **Layered AI review before merge** — every PR gets a [CodeRabbit](https://coderabbit.ai) review plus an independent adversarial Claude review that deliberately runs a different model from the one writing AI-authored changes. On top of that, `main` requires green CI, one approving review, and a human merge. AI agents are structurally barred from editing the workflows, release config, or supply-chain settings that gate them.
- **Inbound issues and PRs are security-triaged** — a read-only AI pass flags code crafted to harm whoever runs it, prompt injection aimed at our own automation, and social engineering. Flagged items are labeled and refused by every AI entry point until a human clears them. It fails closed, so an inconclusive scan flags rather than passes, and the model session itself has no write tools — a separate deterministic step applies the label, so the AI never posts or acts on anything.

Full detail: [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) · [Security guide](https://bestax.io/docs/guides/security)

repository.readme:
Anycon

Run coding agents on your own machine. Talk to them from anywhere.

简体中文

--- Anycon connects the machine that runs your AI agents (a Mac mini at home, a workstation, a server) to a small relay called the **hub**, so you can drive those agents from a browser, your phone, a terminal, or a script, from anywhere. The machine dials out to the hub. You don't need a public IP, a VPN, or port forwarding. ``` your machine hub clients ┌───────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ anycon daemon │ outbound │ anycon-hub │ HTTPS / WS │ Web UI / PWA │ │ ├ Claude Code │ ──────────► │ relays │ ◄─────────────── │ anycon CLI │ │ └ Codex, … │ │ ciphertext │ │ TS SDK │ └───────────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ ▲ ▲ └───────────────── end-to-end encrypted (Noise) ──────────────────┘ ``` ## Why Vendor cloud agents run in the vendor's sandbox: your repo is cloned into a container, dependencies are reinstalled, and your internal services are out of reach. Anycon keeps the agent on **your** machine, with your local databases, GPUs, credentials, and tools already in place, and gives you a remote line to it. - **Self-host first.** The hub is one container and one SQLite file, with no external services. - **The hub only sees metadata.** Session history lives on your machine. Clients and the daemon talk over end-to-end encrypted Noise sessions, and the hub only routes ciphertext and sees metadata. (Read the [privacy model](#privacy-model) for the one big caveat.) - **Agent-agnostic.** Claude Code and Codex work out of the box. More agents can be added through the adapter interface. - **Folders are projects.** Every folder in the workspace directory is a project. Create, clone, or link existing directories from any client. - **A real coding workflow.** Each session can get its own git worktree and branch. You can review diffs, sync with the base branch, approve permission requests, and let the agent commit and open PRs. All of it runs on your machine. - **Protocol first.** The Web UI, CLI, and SDK all use the same public protocol. The trade-offs, stated plainly: - **No isolation.** Agents run as your user on your machine. Workspace boundaries rely on the agent's own permission prompts, not an OS sandbox. - **Your machine has to stay on**, and keeping it online and backed up is up to you. - **The model API still sees your context.** The Claude Code on your machine still sends prompts to its provider. Anycon doesn't change that. **Not in scope:** terminals and remote shells, editors, issue tracking, team collaboration. Dev server previews are tunneled end to end, never proxied through the hub in plaintext (see the privacy model). ## Quick start You need Docker for the hub. The `anycon` binary (daemon and CLI in one) runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Linux (x86_64 and arm64, glibc 2.35 or newer), and Windows (x64, Windows 10 1809 or newer). **Don't want to run a hub yet?** Use the public hub at [hub.anycon.ai](https://hub.anycon.ai): sign in with your email address, then skip to step 2 and use `--hub https://hub.anycon.ai`. The free plan has one node (a machine running the daemon) per account. It runs the same release as a self-hosted hub, but its Web UI's code is served by the hub, so using that Web UI means trusting its operator ([privacy model](#privacy-model)). For anything sensitive, run your own hub or use the CLI / SDK. Its [terms](https://anycon.ai/terms) and [privacy policy](https://anycon.ai/privacy) are on anycon.ai. **1. Run a hub.** It can run on the same machine as the agents, or anywhere both sides can reach. ```bash docker run -d --name anycon-hub -p 8900:8900 -v anycon-data:/data \ -e ANYCON_PUBLIC_URL=https://hub.example.com ghcr.io/anycon-ai/hub:latest docker logs anycon-hub # prints a one-time admin token on first start ``` Want people to sign up on their own (email code or GitHub / Google sign-in, with per-account quotas)? Run it with `ANYCON_MODE=multi`; see [docs/deploy.md § 9](docs/deploy.md#9-公共-hub-与-multi-模式). The image is built for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` and tagged `` (e.g. `0.1.0`), `.` (`0.1`), and `latest`. Pin a version in production. The hub serves plain HTTP. TLS and your domain are handled by your reverse proxy. [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) has ready-to-use configs for Caddy, nginx, Traefik, and Cloudflare Tunnel, plus a [compose file](docker/compose.yml). **2. Install and pair the daemon** on the machine that runs your agents: ```bash brew install anycon-ai/tap/anycon # or, without Homebrew (installs to ~/.local/bin): curl -fsSL https://github.com/anycon-ai/anycon/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh anycon init --hub https://hub.example.com --workspace ~/anycon --name mac-mini --yes anycon daemon # foreground; or `anycon service install` for launchd / systemd anycon pair # in another terminal: prints a 16-character code and a pairing link (--qr for a QR code) ``` On Windows, in PowerShell (installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\anycon\bin` and adds it to your PATH; no administrator rights needed): ```powershell irm https://github.com/anycon-ai/anycon/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex anycon init --hub https://hub.example.com --workspace ~/anycon --name my-pc --yes anycon service install # a scheduled task that starts the daemon at logon, without a console window anycon pair ``` Prebuilt binaries are also attached to each [GitHub release](https://github.com/anycon-ai/anycon/releases), with checksums and build provenance. To build from source instead, run `cargo install --path crates/cli --locked` in a clone (needs a current stable Rust toolchain; on Windows also `cargo install --path crates/windows-launcher --locked` for the console-less launcher the service uses), and `docker build -f docker/hub.Dockerfile -t anycon-hub .` for the hub image. **3. Open the hub in a browser**, sign in with the admin token (on the public hub, with your email), and enter the pairing code. That's it. Every folder under `~/anycon/` is now a project you can work in from the browser. To add another device, use *Add device* in node settings, or run `anycon pair` again. ## Clients **Web UI.** Served by the hub and installable as a PWA. It has streaming Markdown, tool-call rendering, diffs, permission approvals, model / reasoning / permission-mode pickers, per-session worktrees, image and file attachments, and Web Push notifications. Available in English and Chinese. **CLI.** Use it from any terminal: ```bash anycon connect https://hub.example.com --code 7K3P-Q2MX-4FWD-H8RT anycon new --project my-app "run the tests and fix whatever fails" ``` Output streams live, and you answer permission requests right in the terminal. **MCP server.** `anycon mcp` runs an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server on stdio, so another agent can list, read, search, and drive the sessions on your node (set it up as an MCP server with command `anycon` and args `["mcp"]`). It has no tool to approve permission requests, which stay with you; it refuses dangerous permission modes unless you start it with `--allow-dangerous-modes`, and refuses to create or drive sessions from inside an anycon session unless you pass `--allow-nested`. See [ADR-49](docs/decisions.md#adr-49-anycon-mcpstdio-mcp-server-是又一个客户端入口不暴露审批不做编排) and the [CLI spec](docs/spec/cli.md#37-anycon-mcp). **TypeScript SDK** ([`@anycon/sdk`](packages/sdk)): ```ts import { pair, connect } from '@anycon/sdk' await pair('https://hub.example.com', { code: '7K3P-Q2MX-4FWD-H8RT', name: 'ci-runner' }) // once const node = await connect('https://hub.example.com', { node: 'mac-mini' }) const session = await node.sessions.create({ project: 'my-app', agent: 'claude-code' }) for await (const ev of session.send('run the tests and fix whatever fails')) { if (ev.type === 'text_delta') process.stdout.write(ev.text) if (ev.type === 'permission') await ev.allow() } ``` ## Supported agents | Agent | How | |---|---| | Claude Code | Native adapter (bidirectional `stream-json`) | | Codex | Native adapter (`codex app-server`, `codex-cli` ≥ 0.157.0) | | OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Goose, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Pi | [ACP](https://agentclientprotocol.com) v1 adapter (one process per agent, shared by its sessions; the command must already be on the daemon's `PATH`, nothing is fetched with `npx` / `uvx`) | | Mock agent | Deterministic fake agent for development and tests (`ANYCON_MOCK_AGENT=1`) | Installed agents are picked up automatically. Use `anycon config set agents..enabled false` to turn one off (`agents.acp..enabled` for an ACP agent). Any other ACP agent can be added with `anycon config set agents.acp..command ""`. Planned next: custom agents registered as nodes through the SDK. See the [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md). ## Privacy model - Session history is stored **on your machine** (the daemon), never on the hub. - The daemon and every client talk over **Noise end-to-end encryption**. The hub sees metadata: which device talks to which, when, and how many bytes, plus account-level data like device names and account identifiers. - **Accounts hold little.** The hub stores a display name, an email if you bound one (or one that GitHub / Google reported as verified), the provider and stable user ID of any linked GitHub / Google account (no username, avatar, or access token), your device list, and audit records such as sign-ins. An email the provider has not verified is never used to match or create an account. You can delete your account in settings: the hub removes those records (devices, pairings, sign-in methods, audit rows) and keeps only a deletion record without an IP address. Session history was never on the hub, so it is unaffected. - **The Web UI's code is served by the hub.** A malicious or compromised hub could serve modified JavaScript and read keys and plaintext in your browser. Using the Web UI therefore means trusting the operator of that hub. For sensitive use, **self-host the hub**, or use the **CLI / SDK**, whose code you install yourself. - Pairing codes are generated on the daemon and never sent to the hub. Both sides derive the pre-shared key from the code with Argon2id. The default 16-character code holds up against offline guessing even by a malicious hub. Use the 8-character `anycon pair --short` only with a hub you run yourself. - Browser keys and caches are stored unencrypted in IndexedDB. That includes the titles and notes of your to-do items (the local copy of the list and any changes not yet sent to the node), with the same exposure as the session cache. What clears what: *Sign out* clears nothing on disk. *Sign out and remove this device* deletes the whole local database, including the to-do cache, queued changes and any shared text not yet picked up. Forgetting a node deletes that node's cached to-dos and its queued changes. Signing in as a different account wipes all local data, including a share that was never picked up. On a shared computer, use *Sign out and remove this device*, not just *Sign out*. - **Sharing text into the Web UI.** When the installed web app receives a share from another app, its service worker handles it: the shared text is kept in a small browser database, never put in a URL, and nothing is added to your list until you confirm. When no service worker with that handler is in control (none is active yet; an older version without the handler is still in control, which is the case for every existing user until they accept the update or close every window and tab of the app, since a reload does not activate a waiting service worker; or service workers are unavailable or disabled in the browser), that one request reaches the hub instead. The hub answers with a redirect and discards the body without parsing, storing or logging it, but the shared text did pass through the hub, and through any TLS-terminating proxy in front of it, which can see the body. - **Dev server previews** run on a separate domain (on the public hub, `*.aiplace.app`) and travel through their own Noise tunnel to the daemon. The hub sees that a preview is open and how much traffic it carries, not the pages. The preview loader is also served by the hub, so the same trust caveat as the Web UI applies. By default the daemon only forwards to ports opened by an agent session. - **An agent you wire to `anycon mcp` acts with the permissions of your CLI** (by default the local daemon's socket; with `--node` / `--hub`, the CLI device this machine has paired). The MCP server exposes eleven tools that map onto existing requests, and its limits sit on that interface: no tool approves or denies a permission request (a call that reaches one returns `waiting_permission` for a person to handle on a paired device); `create_session` refuses permission modes marked dangerous and `send_message` refuses sessions already in one, unless you start the server with `--allow-dangerous-modes` (the node's `permissions.allow_dangerous_modes` still applies); there is no session `env`; and inside an agent that anycon started, creating, driving and cancelling sessions is refused unless you pass `--allow-nested`. These are guardrails on the interface, not isolation: an agent can change its own environment and MCP configuration, and one that can run shell commands can run `anycon` itself. Actions that come through it are recorded as `local-mcp` in the audit log. - **Agents can add to your to-do list, and only add.** The MCP tool `add_todo`, and `anycon todo add` run inside an agent that anycon started, put an item on the node's to-do list without `--allow-nested`. Such an item is marked as added by an agent and as unreviewed until you look at it, and the node keeps at most 100 of those. An agent cannot change, close or delete items through these interfaces (the MCP server has no tool for it, and `anycon todo done` / `drop` / `reopen` / `rm` refuse inside an agent session). The agent marking is self-reported, so it is a guardrail: a process that deliberately hides where it comes from, or any shell on a machine whose CLI is paired with the node, can add items that look like yours and can change the list. To-do titles and notes are your content: they are stored in plain text in the daemon's database, like session history, and travel only over the end-to-end channel, so the hub sees only metadata such as message sizes and timing. - **Handing a to-do to an agent passes earlier agents' output on.** When you dispatch a to-do item (`anycon todo run`, `todo.dispatch`), the node opens a session for it and, at the end of each turn, records the agent's last text (up to 4 KiB) on the item. When you dispatch the same item again, the reports of the last five dispatches (up to 8 KiB in all) are put into the new session's first message, labelled as reports from earlier sessions and not as instructions. A session that was hit by a prompt injection can therefore write text that reaches the next agent's input. The label (and the `> ` prefix on every line of a report) is a hint, not a defence against injection. The node generates that message itself and refuses `todo.dispatch` from a connection that declared itself `mcp`, and `anycon todo run` refuses inside an agent session that anycon started; both are guard rails, not a boundary, so an agent with a shell can still dispatch. The recorded text is session content: it stays out of logs and the audit log, and it travels only over the end-to-end channel (the hub sees only metadata such as message sizes and timing). Dispatches start with the agent's "no push, no pull request" option on where the agent has one (Claude Code does, as permission rules on `git push`, `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge`). That is a command-pattern guard rail, not a boundary: a script that pushes gets through. Agents that do not have the option (Codex, ACP agents) can be dispatched to only if you explicitly give it up. - Anycon is not a sandbox (see the trade-offs above). The full threat model is in [docs/architecture.md § 5.6](docs/architecture.md#56-威胁模型) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation | | | |---|---| | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | Components, data ownership, encryption, workspaces | | [Protocol](docs/protocol.md) | Envelopes, pairing handshake, JSON-RPC methods, offline behavior | | [Specs](docs/spec/) | What the daemon, hub, Web UI, CLI, and SDK do in detail | | [Deployment](docs/deploy.md) | Self-hosting, reverse proxies, backups, upgrades | | [Decisions](docs/decisions.md) | Architecture decision records | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | What's in v0.1 and what's next | The design docs are in Chinese for now. English versions will follow once v0.1 settles. ## Development Toolchain versions are pinned in [`mise.toml`](mise.toml) (Rust, bun, Node, just). ```bash bun install just gen-wasm && bun run --cwd web build # first time: Noise wasm + Web UI (embedded into the hub) just dev # hub :8900 + daemon (mock agent) + Web dev server :5173 just test # Rust + TypeScript tests just lint # fmt, clippy, oxlint, typecheck just e2e # Playwright against a real hub + daemon + Web UI ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the dev loop, conventions, and where help is most welcome. ## Status Anycon is at **v0.2**. The core flow works end to end and has automated tests: run a hub, pair, chat with an agent, approve permissions, work in worktrees. The protocol and APIs may still change between minor versions. Please report bugs and rough edges in [issues](https://github.com/anycon-ai/anycon/issues), and send security problems to the channel in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE)

sampled_files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
# CI：Rust（macOS / Linux / Windows）、hub 的 Postgres 存储、TS、生成产物检查、E2E（Playwright + SDK 对真实 hub/daemon）、Docker 构建（自包含 Dockerfile）；
# main 上全部通过后推 edge 镜像。
# 本地等价命令：`just lint`、`just test`、`just gen-check`、`just e2e`、`just test-sdk-real`、`just docker-hub`。
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0

jobs:
  rust:
    name: rust (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - name: cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --workspace
      # 进程内 hub + 真实 daemon 子进程（mock agent）+ CLI 客户端的 happy path；workspace 测试里已包含，单列一步方便看结果。
      - name: happy path（hub + daemon + CLI 端到端）
        run: cargo test -p anycon-cli --test happy_path
      - name: crypto wasm 目标能编译
        run: cargo check -p anycon-crypto --features wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown

  # Windows：daemon + CLI（命名管道、Job Object、计划任务，ADR-42）。hub 只发 Linux 镜像，但 CLI 的集成测试在进程内起 hub，所以整个
  # workspace 都要能编译、能测。依赖 sh 脚本 / 伪终端 / unix 权限位的测试在代码里用 `cfg(unix)` 跳过。
  rust-windows:
    name: rust (windows-latest)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    env:
      # aws-lc-sys 在 x86_64 Windows 上要 NASM；runner 上没有，用它自带的预编译目标文件
      AWS_LC_SYS_PREBUILT_NASM: "1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
      # 不在第一个失败的测试二进制处停下：Windows 上的失败往往互不相关，一次看全
      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast
      - name: happy path（hub + daemon + CLI 端到端，经命名管道）
        run: cargo test -p anycon-cli --test happy_path

  # hub 的 Postgres 存储（ADR-12）：store 的共用测试和依赖 store 的集成测试在真实的 Postgres 上再跑一遍（设了
  # ANYCON_TEST_POSTGRES_URL 才会跑；`rust` job 里没设，Postgres 那一遍直接跳过）。每个用例在库里建自己的 schema，跑完删掉。
  # 版本：只跑 Postgres 18，别的版本没有验证。本地怎么跑见 CONTRIBUTING.md「提交前」。
  hub-postgres:
    name: hub (postgres 18)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:18
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: anycon
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: anycon
          POSTGRES_DB: anycon
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U anycon -d anycon"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 20
    env:
      ANYCON_TEST_POSTGRES_URL: postgres://anycon:anycon@localhost:5432/anycon
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: cargo test -p anycon-hub（SQLite 和 Postgres 各一遍）
        run: cargo test -p anycon-hub

  ts:
    name: ts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.x
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
      # wasm 产物（packages/protocol/wasm）让 protocol / sdk 的测试跑真实 Noise 而不只是 mock，也是 web 构建的输入。
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: just,wasm-pack
      - name: bun 安装缓存
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: bun-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            bun-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: bun.lock 里没有非默认 registry 的地址
        run: |
          if grep -E '"https://registry\.' bun.lock | grep -v 'registry\.npmjs\.org'; then
            echo "bun.lock 含非默认 registry 地址：本地跑 \`just lock-clean\` 后再提交" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: 构建 wasm
        run: just gen-wasm
      - name: lint
        run: bun run lint
      - name: 格式检查（oxfmt）
        run: bun run fmt:check
      - name: typecheck
        run: bun run typecheck
      - name: test（bun）
        run: bun run test
      - name: test（Node 运行时）
        run: |
          bun run --cwd packages/protocol test:node
          bun run --cwd packages/sdk test:node
      - name: build 包
        run: |
          bun run --cwd packages/protocol build
          bun run --cwd packages/sdk build
      - name: build web
        if: hashFiles('web/package.json') != ''
        run: bun run --cwd web build

  gen-check:
    name: gen-check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.x
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: just
      - name: bun 安装缓存
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: bun-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            bun-${{ runner.os }}-
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: 重新生成 schema 和 TS 类型
        run: just gen
      - name: 重新生成 msgpack / JSON-RPC 测试向量
        run: just gen-vectors
      - name: 产物无 diff
        run: git diff --exit-code -- schema packages/protocol/src/generated.ts packages/protocol/src/method-types.ts packages/protocol/tests/vectors

  e2e:
    name: e2e
    needs: [rust, ts]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # daemon 默认启动时要跑 `$SHELL -ilc` 解析登录环境；CI 里没有用户 rc，关掉省几秒（测试夹具也各自设了一遍）。
      ANYCON_AGENTS__ENV_FROM_LOGIN_SHELL: "false"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.x
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: just,wasm-pack
      - name: bun 安装缓存
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: bun-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            bun-${{ runner.os }}-
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      # 顺序很重要：wasm → web → cargo。hub 的 build.rs 在编译时选中 web/dist 嵌入，web 又依赖 wasm。
      - name: 1. 构建 wasm
        run: just gen-wasm
      - name: 2. build web
        if: hashFiles('web/package.json') != ''
        run: bun run --cwd web build
      - name: 3. build hub + cli
        run: cargo build -p anycon-hub -p anycon-cli
      # SDK 对真实 hub + daemon（mock agent）：pair → connect → send → 权限 → history → cancel。
      - name: SDK 对真实 hub + daemon
        run: just test-sdk-real
      - name: Playwright 浏览器缓存
        id: playwright-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
      - name: 安装 chromium（缓存未命中）
        if: steps.playwright-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        working-directory: e2e
        run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: 安装 chromium 的系统依赖（缓存命中）
        if: steps.playwright-cache.outputs.cache-hit == 'true'
        working-directory: e2e
        run: bunx playwright install-deps chromium
      - name: playwright
        env:
          E2E_REQUIRE_DAEMON: "1"
          # 失败时要看 hub / daemon 的日志：保留临时目录，路径写到已知文件里（下一步按它收集）
          E2E_KEEP_TMP: "1"
          E2E_TMP_DIR_FILE: ${{ runner.temp }}/e2e-tmp-dir
          # hub 和 daemon 都读它（global-setup 把环境传给两者）。debug 级也只有元数据：设备 id、seq、长度、方法名、耗时，
          # 没有会话内容（hub 不解析 payload；daemon 的 debug 日志不打印消息、工具输出或 RPC 参数）
          ANYCON_LOG: info,anycon_hub=debug,anycon_daemon=debug
        run: bun run --cwd e2e test
      - name: 收集 hub / daemon 日志（含 multi 用例自己起的 hub）
        if: failure()
        run: |
          mkdir -p e2e/ci-logs
          dir=$(cat "${{ runner.temp }}/e2e-tmp-dir" 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -d "$dir" ]; then
            # 只拿这两个日志：临时目录里还有 daemon 的密钥、hub 的数据库和管理员 token，不进产物
            for f in hub.log daemon.log; do
              if [ -f "$dir/$f" ]; then cp "$dir/$f" e2e/ci-logs/; fi
            done
            # multi 模式的用例自己起的 hub（e2e/helpers/multi-hub.ts）：目录在主临时目录下的 m<序号>（m1…），日志是 m<序号>/hub.log
            for d in "$dir"/m[0-9]*/; do
              if [ -f "${d}hub.log" ]; then cp "${d}hub.log" "e2e/ci-logs/multi-$(basename "$d")-hub.log"; fi
            done
          else
            echo "e2e tmp dir not found (global-setup did not get that far?)"
          fi
          ls -la e2e/ci-logs
      - name: 上传报告
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6
        with:
          name: e2e-report
          path: |
            e2e/playwright-report
            e2e/test-results
            e2e/ci-logs
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  docker:
    name: docker (hub image)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
      # docker/hub.Dockerfile 是自包含的：wasm（wasm-bindgen-cli）→ Web UI（bun + vite）→ hub（嵌入 Web UI）→ distroless。
      # 用默认基础镜像；Docker Hub 连不上的机器本地换源见 `just docker-hub` 的注释。
      - name: 构建（不推送）
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          file: docker/hub.Dockerfile
          push: false
          load: true
          tags: anycon-hub:ci
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
      - name: 容器起得来，/healthz 200，提供的是真正的 Web UI
        run: |
          docker run -d --name hub -p 127.0.0.1:8900:8900 -v anycon-ci-data:/data \
            -e ANYCON_PUBLIC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8900 \
            -e 'ANYCON_PREVIEW_URL=http://*.preview.localhost:8900' anycon-hub:ci
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8900/healthz; then break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8900/healthz
          echo
          # 不是 crates/hub/static-placeholder 的占位页，而是嵌进去的 web/dist（有 #root 和带哈希的入口脚本）。
          curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8900/ > index.html
          grep -q 'id="root"' index.html
          if grep -q 'does not include the web UI' index.html; then echo "hub embeds the placeholder page, not the web UI" >&2; exit 1; fi
          asset=$(grep -o '/assets/[^"]*\.js' index.html | head -1)
          curl -fsS -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8900${asset}"
          # 真实 Noise wasm 在产物里：web 构建缺 wasm 时 vite 会换成桩，所以显式确认它被嵌进来并以 application/wasm 提供。
          # service worker 的预缓存清单（/sw.js）列出了全部产物，包括带哈希的 wasm。
          wasm=$(curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8900/sw.js | grep -o 'assets/anycon_crypto_bg-[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.wasm' | head -1)
          test -n "$wasm"
          curl -fsS -D headers.txt -o wasm.bin "http://127.0.0.1:8900/${wasm}"
          grep -qi '^content-type: application/wasm' headers.txt
          test "$(wc -c < wasm.bin)" -gt 100000
          # 预览运行时（ADR-39）是第二份嵌入：预览域名上的引导页不是 static-placeholder-preview，
          # sw.js 带 Service-Worker-Allowed，主域名上取不到它们。
          preview_host='aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.preview.localhost:8900'
          curl -fsS -H "Host: $preview_host" http://127.0.0.1:8900/__anycon/enter > enter.html
          if grep -q 'The preview runtime is not built into this hub' enter.html; then echo "hub embeds the preview placeholder" >&2; exit 1; fi
          grep -q '/__anycon/' enter.html
          curl -fsS -D sw-headers.txt -o /dev/null -H "Host: $preview_host" http://127.0.0.1:8900/__anycon/sw.js
          grep -qi '^service-worker-allowed: /' sw-headers.txt
          test "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8900/__anycon/sw.js)" = 404
          # 镜像自带的 HEALTHCHECK（distroless 里没有 curl）也要变成 healthy
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if [ "$(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}' hub)" = healthy ]; then exit 0; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          docker logs hub
          exit 1

  # main 上全部检查通过后推 ghcr.io/anycon-ai/hub:edge 和 :sha-<短 sha>，给要跟着 main 跑的自建 hub 用（docs/deploy.md 开头）。
  # 只有 amd64：arm64 要原生 runner 从头编 Rust，跟 main 的场景不值得；正式版的多架构镜像由 release.yml 出。
  # docker job 刚用同一个 Dockerfile 写了 gha 缓存，这里基本全部命中，不重新编译。
  edge:
    name: docker (edge image)
    needs: [rust, rust-windows, hub-postgres, ts, gen-check, e2e, docker]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: 标签
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v6
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/anycon-ai/hub
          flavor: |
            latest=false
          tags: |
            type=edge,branch=main
            type=sha,format=short,prefix=sha-
          labels: |
            org.opencontainers.image.title=anycon-hub
            org.opencontainers.image.description=Anycon hub (edge, built from main; not a release)
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
      - name: 登录 GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: 构建并推送
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          file: docker/hub.Dockerfile
          platforms: linux/amd64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha

sampled_files.README.md:
Anycon

Run coding agents on your own machine. Talk to them from anywhere.

简体中文

--- Anycon connects the machine that runs your AI agents (a Mac mini at home, a workstation, a server) to a small relay called the **hub**, so you can drive those agents from a browser, your phone, a terminal, or a script, from anywhere. The machine dials out to the hub. You don't need a public IP, a VPN, or port forwarding. ``` your machine hub clients ┌───────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ anycon daemon │ outbound │ anycon-hub │ HTTPS / WS │ Web UI / PWA │ │ ├ Claude Code │ ──────────► │ relays │ ◄─────────────── │ anycon CLI │ │ └ Codex, … │ │ ciphertext │ │ TS SDK │ └───────────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ ▲ ▲ └───────────────── end-to-end encrypted (Noise) ──────────────────┘ ``` ## Why Vendor cloud agents run in the vendor's sandbox: your repo is cloned into a container, dependencies are reinstalled, and your internal services are out of reach. Anycon keeps the agent on **your** machine, with your local databases, GPUs, credentials, and tools already in place, and gives you a remote line to it. - **Self-host first.** The hub is one container and one SQLite file, with no external services. - **The hub only sees metadata.** Session history lives on your machine. Clients and the daemon talk over end-to-end encrypted Noise sessions, and the hub only routes ciphertext and sees metadata. (Read the [privacy model](#privacy-model) for the one big caveat.) - **Agent-agnostic.** Claude Code and Codex work out of the box. More agents can be added through the adapter interface. - **Folders are projects.** Every folder in the workspace directory is a project. Create, clone, or link existing directories from any client. - **A real coding workflow.** Each session can get its own git worktree and branch. You can review diffs, sync with the base branch, approve permission requests, and let the agent commit and open PRs. All of it runs on your machine. - **Protocol first.** The Web UI, CLI, and SDK all use the same public protocol. The trade-offs, stated plainly: - **No isolation.** Agents run as your user on your machine. Workspace boundaries rely on the agent's own permission prompts, not an OS sandbox. - **Your machine has to stay on**, and keeping it online and backed up is up to you. - **The model API still sees your context.** The Claude Code on your machine still sends prompts to its provider. Anycon doesn't change that. **Not in scope:** terminals and remote shells, editors, issue tracking, team collaboration. Dev server previews are tunneled end to end, never proxied through the hub in plaintext (see the privacy model). ## Quick start You need Docker for the hub. The `anycon` binary (daemon and CLI in one) runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Linux (x86_64 and arm64, glibc 2.35 or newer), and Windows (x64, Windows 10 1809 or newer). **Don't want to run a hub yet?** Use the public hub at [hub.anycon.ai](https://hub.anycon.ai): sign in with your email address, then skip to step 2 and use `--hub https://hub.anycon.ai`. The free plan has one node (a machine running the daemon) per account. It runs the same release as a self-hosted hub, but its Web UI's code is served by the hub, so using that Web UI means trusting its operator ([privacy model](#privacy-model)). For anything sensitive, run your own hub or use the CLI / SDK. Its [terms](https://anycon.ai/terms) and [privacy policy](https://anycon.ai/privacy) are on anycon.ai. **1. Run a hub.** It can run on the same machine as the agents, or anywhere both sides can reach. ```bash docker run -d --name anycon-hub -p 8900:8900 -v anycon-data:/data \ -e ANYCON_PUBLIC_URL=https://hub.example.com ghcr.io/anycon-ai/hub:latest docker logs anycon-hub # prints a one-time admin token on first start ``` Want people to sign up on their own (email code or GitHub / Google sign-in, with per-account quotas)? Run it with `ANYCON_MODE=multi`; see [docs/deploy.md § 9](docs/deploy.md#9-公共-hub-与-multi-模式). The image is built for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` and tagged `` (e.g. `0.1.0`), `.` (`0.1`), and `latest`. Pin a version in production. The hub serves plain HTTP. TLS and your domain are handled by your reverse proxy. [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) has ready-to-use configs for Caddy, nginx, Traefik, and Cloudflare Tunnel, plus a [compose file](docker/compose.yml). **2. Install and pair the daemon** on the machine that runs your agents: ```bash brew install anycon-ai/tap/anycon # or, without Homebrew (installs to ~/.local/bin): curl -fsSL https://github.com/anycon-ai/anycon/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh anycon init --hub https://hub.example.com --workspace ~/anycon --name mac-mini --yes anycon daemon # foreground; or `anycon service install` for launchd / systemd anycon pair # in another terminal: prints a 16-character code and a pairing link (--qr for a QR code) ``` On Windows, in PowerShell (installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\anycon\bin` and adds it to your PATH; no administrator rights needed): ```powershell irm https://github.com/anycon-ai/anycon/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex anycon init --hub https://hub.example.com --workspace ~/anycon --name my-pc --yes anycon service install # a scheduled task that starts the daemon at logon, without a console window anycon pair ``` Prebuilt binaries are also attached to each [GitHub release](https://github.com/anycon-ai/anycon/releases), with checksums and build provenance. To build from source instead, run `cargo install --path crates/cli --locked` in a clone (needs a current stable Rust toolchain; on Windows also `cargo install --path crates/windows-launcher --locked` for the console-less launcher the service uses), and `docker build -f docker/hub.Dockerfile -t anycon-hub .` for the hub image. **3. Open the hub in a browser**, sign in with the admin token (on the public hub, with your email), and enter the pairing code. That's it. Every folder under `~/anycon/` is now a project you can work in from the browser. To add another device, use *Add device* in node settings, or run `anycon pair` again. ## Clients **Web UI.** Served by the hub and installable as a PWA. It has streaming Markdown, tool-call rendering, diffs, permission approvals, model / reasoning / permission-mode pickers, per-session worktrees, image and file attachments, and Web Push notifications. Available in English and Chinese. **CLI.** Use it from any terminal: ```bash anycon connect https://hub.example.com --code 7K3P-Q2MX-4FWD-H8RT anycon new --project my-app "run the tests and fix whatever fails" ``` Output streams live, and you answer permission requests right in the terminal. **MCP server.** `anycon mcp` runs an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server on stdio, so another agent can list, read, search, and drive the sessions on your node (set it up as an MCP server with command `anycon` and args `["mcp"]`). It has no tool to approve permission requests, which stay with you; it refuses dangerous permission modes unless you start it with `--allow-dangerous-modes`, and refuses to create or drive sessions from inside an anycon session unless you pass `--allow-nested`. See [ADR-49](docs/decisions.md#adr-49-anycon-mcpstdio-mcp-server-是又一个客户端入口不暴露审批不做编排) and the [CLI spec](docs/spec/cli.md#37-anycon-mcp). **TypeScript SDK** ([`@anycon/sdk`](packages/sdk)): ```ts import { pair, connect } from '@anycon/sdk' await pair('https://hub.example.com', { code: '7K3P-Q2MX-4FWD-H8RT', name: 'ci-runner' }) // once const node = await connect('https://hub.example.com', { node: 'mac-mini' }) const session = await node.sessions.create({ project: 'my-app', agent: 'claude-code' }) for await (const ev of session.send('run the tests and fix whatever fails')) { if (ev.type === 'text_delta') process.stdout.write(ev.text) if (ev.type === 'permission') await ev.allow() } ``` ## Supported agents | Agent | How | |---|---| | Claude Code | Native adapter (bidirectional `stream-json`) | | Codex | Native adapter (`codex app-server`, `codex-cli` ≥ 0.157.0) | | OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Goose, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Pi | [ACP](https://agentclientprotocol.com) v1 adapter (one process per agent, shared by its sessions; the command must already be on the daemon's `PATH`, nothing is fetched with `npx` / `uvx`) | | Mock agent | Deterministic fake agent for development and tests (`ANYCON_MOCK_AGENT=1`) | Installed agents are picked up automatically. Use `anycon config set agents..enabled false` to turn one off (`agents.acp..enabled` for an ACP agent). Any other ACP agent can be added with `anycon config set agents.acp..command ""`. Planned next: custom agents registered as nodes through the SDK. See the [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md). ## Privacy model - Session history is stored **on your machine** (the daemon), never on the hub. - The daemon and every client talk over **Noise end-to-end encryption**. The hub sees metadata: which device talks to which, when, and how many bytes, plus account-level data like device names and account identifiers. - **Accounts hold little.** The hub stores a display name, an email if you bound one (or one that GitHub / Google reported as verified), the provider and stable user ID of any linked GitHub / Google account (no username, avatar, or access token), your device list, and audit records such as sign-ins. An email the provider has not verified is never used to match or create an account. You can delete your account in settings: the hub removes those records (devices, pairings, sign-in methods, audit rows) and keeps only a deletion record without an IP address. Session history was never on the hub, so it is unaffected. - **The Web UI's code is served by the hub.** A malicious or compromised hub could serve modified JavaScript and read keys and plaintext in your browser. Using the Web UI therefore means trusting the operator of that hub. For sensitive use, **self-host the hub**, or use the **CLI / SDK**, whose code you install yourself. - Pairing codes are generated on the daemon and never sent to the hub. Both sides derive the pre-shared key from the code with Argon2id. The default 16-character code holds up against offline guessing even by a malicious hub. Use the 8-character `anycon pair --short` only with a hub you run yourself. - Browser keys and caches are stored unencrypted in IndexedDB. That includes the titles and notes of your to-do items (the local copy of the list and any changes not yet sent to the node), with the same exposure as the session cache. What clears what: *Sign out* clears nothing on disk. *Sign out and remove this device* deletes the whole local database, including the to-do cache, queued changes and any shared text not yet picked up. Forgetting a node deletes that node's cached to-dos and its queued changes. Signing in as a different account wipes all local data, including a share that was never picked up. On a shared computer, use *Sign out and remove this device*, not just *Sign out*. - **Sharing text into the Web UI.** When the installed web app receives a share from another app, its service worker handles it: the shared text is kept in a small browser database, never put in a URL, and nothing is added to your list until you confirm. When no service worker with that handler is in control (none is active yet; an older version without the handler is still in control, which is the case for every existing user until they accept the update or close every window and tab of the app, since a reload does not activate a waiting service worker; or service workers are unavailable or disabled in the browser), that one request reaches the hub instead. The hub answers with a redirect and discards the body without parsing, storing or logging it, but the shared text did pass through the hub, and through any TLS-terminating proxy in front of it, which can see the body. - **Dev server previews** run on a separate domain (on the public hub, `*.aiplace.app`) and travel through their own Noise tunnel to the daemon. The hub sees that a preview is open and how much traffic it carries, not the pages. The preview loader is also served by the hub, so the same trust caveat as the Web UI applies. By default the daemon only forwards to ports opened by an agent session. - **An agent you wire to `anycon mcp` acts with the permissions of your CLI** (by default the local daemon's socket; with `--node` / `--hub`, the CLI device this machine has paired). The MCP server exposes eleven tools that map onto existing requests, and its limits sit on that interface: no tool approves or denies a permission request (a call that reaches one returns `waiting_permission` for a person to handle on a paired device); `create_session` refuses permission modes marked dangerous and `send_message` refuses sessions already in one, unless you start the server with `--allow-dangerous-modes` (the node's `permissions.allow_dangerous_modes` still applies); there is no session `env`; and inside an agent that anycon started, creating, driving and cancelling sessions is refused unless you pass `--allow-nested`. These are guardrails on the interface, not isolation: an agent can change its own environment and MCP configuration, and one that can run shell commands can run `anycon` itself. Actions that come through it are recorded as `local-mcp` in the audit log. - **Agents can add to your to-do list, and only add.** The MCP tool `add_todo`, and `anycon todo add` run inside an agent that anycon started, put an item on the node's to-do list without `--allow-nested`. Such an item is marked as added by an agent and as unreviewed until you look at it, and the node keeps at most 100 of those. An agent cannot change, close or delete items through these interfaces (the MCP server has no tool for it, and `anycon todo done` / `drop` / `reopen` / `rm` refuse inside an agent session). The agent marking is self-reported, so it is a guardrail: a process that deliberately hides where it comes from, or any shell on a machine whose CLI is paired with the node, can add items that look like yours and can change the list. To-do titles and notes are your content: they are stored in plain text in the daemon's database, like session history, and travel only over the end-to-end channel, so the hub sees only metadata such as message sizes and timing. - **Handing a to-do to an agent passes earlier agents' output on.** When you dispatch a to-do item (`anycon todo run`, `todo.dispatch`), the node opens a session for it and, at the end of each turn, records the agent's last text (up to 4 KiB) on the item. When you dispatch the same item again, the reports of the last five dispatches (up to 8 KiB in all) are put into the new session's first message, labelled as reports from earlier sessions and not as instructions. A session that was hit by a prompt injection can therefore write text that reaches the next agent's input. The label (and the `> ` prefix on every line of a report) is a hint, not a defence against injection. The node generates that message itself and refuses `todo.dispatch` from a connection that declared itself `mcp`, and `anycon todo run` refuses inside an agent session that anycon started; both are guard rails, not a boundary, so an agent with a shell can still dispatch. The recorded text is session content: it stays out of logs and the audit log, and it travels only over the end-to-end channel (the hub sees only metadata such as message sizes and timing). Dispatches start with the agent's "no push, no pull request" option on where the agent has one (Claude Code does, as permission rules on `git push`, `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge`). That is a command-pattern guard rail, not a boundary: a script that pushes gets through. Agents that do not have the option (Codex, ACP agents) can be dispatched to only if you explicitly give it up. - Anycon is not a sandbox (see the trade-offs above). The full threat model is in [docs/architecture.md § 5.6](docs/architecture.md#56-威胁模型) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation | | | |---|---| | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | Components, data ownership, encryption, workspaces | | [Protocol](docs/protocol.md) | Envelopes, pairing handshake, JSON-RPC methods, offline behavior | | [Specs](docs/spec/) | What the daemon, hub, Web UI, CLI, and SDK do in detail | | [Deployment](docs/deploy.md) | Self-hosting, reverse proxies, backups, upgrades | | [Decisions](docs/decisions.md) | Architecture decision records | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | What's in v0.1 and what's next | The design docs are in Chinese for now. English versions will follow once v0.1 settles. ## Development Toolchain versions are pinned in [`mise.toml`](mise.toml) (Rust, bun, Node, just). ```bash bun install just gen-wasm && bun run --cwd web build # first time: Noise wasm + Web UI (embedded into the hub) just dev # hub :8900 + daemon (mock agent) + Web dev server :5173 just test # Rust + TypeScript tests just lint # fmt, clippy, oxlint, typecheck just e2e # Playwright against a real hub + daemon + Web UI ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the dev loop, conventions, and where help is most welcome. ## Status Anycon is at **v0.2**. The core flow works end to end and has automated tests: run a hub, pair, chat with an agent, approve permissions, work in worktrees. The protocol and APIs may still change between minor versions. Please report bugs and rough edges in [issues](https://github.com/anycon-ai/anycon/issues), and send security problems to the channel in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE)

repository.readme:
# 智码 AICoder

> 一站式 AI 编程助手管理平台 — 支持 Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI

## 简介

智码 AICoder 是一款轻量级桌面应用，为 AI CLI 编程工具打造统一管理平台。支持 **Claude Code**、**Codex CLI**、**Gemini CLI** 三大 AI 编程助手，提供可视化的会话管理、多标签终端、Token 统计和开发效率工具，让你在一个桌面应用中高效管理所有 AI 编程工作流。

## 应用预览

### 主界面 — 多项目会话管理 + 快捷键面板

![主界面](screenshots/1.jpg)

### 多标签终端 — 代码 Diff 视图 + 多项目会话管理

![多标签终端](screenshots/2.jpg)

### 项目右键菜单 — 导入导出 / 记忆管理 / 文件操作

![项目菜单](screenshots/3.jpg)

### 状态栏 — Token 用量统计 + 会话耗时追踪

![状态栏](screenshots/4.jpg)

### 设置面板 — API 配置 / CLI 工具管理 / 版本切换

![设置面板](screenshots/5.jpg)

### 内置浏览器 — 分屏预览网页应用

![内置浏览器](screenshots/6.jpg)

## 核心功能

- **多工具统一管理** — 支持 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Gemini CLI，自动检测已安装工具和版本，一键切换
- **终端管理** — 内置 PTY 终端，支持多标签页并行会话，会话可弹出为独立窗口
- **会话管理** — 创建、切换、收藏会话，按项目自动分组，8 种颜色标记，模糊搜索秒找历史对话
- **多账号隔离** — 多实例完全独立（登录凭据/API Key/会话记录/配置），支持同时使用公司和个人账号
- **Claude 会话浏览** — 查看历史对话记录，支持搜索和导出（Markdown/HTML），自动生成会话摘要
- **Token 统计** — 实时追踪 API 用量（输入/输出/缓存分别统计），每日趋势图 + 月度总览 + 180 天热力图
- **代码片段** — 保存常用 Prompt 和代码模板，支持模板变量，一键插入终端
- **AI 记忆管理** — 支持多 AI 提供商的记忆生成和管理
- **快捷命令面板** — `Ctrl+K` 整合内置指令、项目命令、代码片段，智能排序
- **内置浏览器** — 分屏预览网页应用
- **文件浏览器** — 树形浏览项目文件，20+ 种文件类型图标
- **Git 面板** — 查看当前分支、提交日志、文件变更状态
- **API 配置管理** — 多 API Profile 切换，支持不同密钥和端点配置
- **MCP Server 管理** — 可视化管理 Model Context Protocol 服务器配置
- **CLAUDE.md 编辑器** — 项目级和全局 CLAUDE.md 在线编辑
- **深色/浅色主题** — 跟随系统或手动切换，护眼舒适
- **系统托盘** — 最小化到托盘，常驻后台
- **自动更新** — 内置 OTA 更新，新版本自动推送
- **零额外开销** — CLI 原生运行，不拦截/不修改/不转发 API 请求，费用与直接用终端完全一样

## 系统要求

- **操作系统**: Windows 10/11 (x64)、macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel)
- **运行时**: 无需额外安装（Windows WebView2 已内置于 Windows 10+）
- **磁盘**: ~10 MB 安装空间
- **前置**: 需已安装以下至少一个 AI CLI 工具：
  - [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code)（Anthropic）
  - [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex)（OpenAI）
  - [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli)（Google）

## 下载安装

### 最新版本: v6.6.0

> 🔐 **本版本 Windows 安装包已正规 EV 代码签名**，消除 Windows 智能应用控制的「未验证开发者」提示。
> 🍎 **macOS 安装包已 Developer ID 签名并通过 Apple 公证**，双架构均为 Accepted。
> 📌 **版本号规则自 v5.0.0 起变更**：每一位满 10 进 1（5.0.0 → 5.0.9 → 5.1.0 → … → 5.9.9 → 6.0.0），不再出现 4.55.0 这样的两位数段。

| 平台 | 下载链接 |
|------|---------|
| Windows x64 | [AICoder_6.6.0_x64-setup.exe](https://pub-9d9e6c0cb6934fb0a0c505e3c64f39b2.r2.dev/aicoder/releases/v6.6.0/AICoder_6.6.0_x64-setup.exe) |
| macOS Apple Silicon | [AICoder_6.6.0_aarch64.dmg](https://pub-9d9e6c0cb6934fb0a0c505e3c64f39b2.r2.dev/aicoder/releases/v6.6.0/AICoder_6.6.0_aarch64.dmg) |
| macOS Intel | [AICoder_6.6.0_x64.dmg](https://pub-9d9e6c0cb6934fb0a0c505e3c64f39b2.r2.dev/aicoder/releases/v6.6.0/AICoder_6.6.0_x64.dmg) |
| Linux Debian/Ubuntu ⭐ **推荐** | [AICoder_6.6.0_amd64.deb](https://pub-9d9e6c0cb6934fb0a0c505e3c64f39b2.r2.dev/aicoder/releases/v6.6.0/AICoder_6.6.0_amd64.deb) |
| Linux AppImage（仅 22.04 一带旧发行版） | [AICoder_6.6.0_amd64.AppImage](https://pub-9d9e6c0cb6934fb0a0c505e3c64f39b2.r2.dev/aicoder/releases/v6.6.0/AICoder_6.6.0_amd64.AppImage) |

> 🐧 **Linux 用户请优先用 `.deb`**。AppImage 在 Ubuntu 22.04 上构建、捆绑了当时的 glib / WebKitGTK，
> 在 **Ubuntu 24.04+ 上会因符号不匹配直接崩溃**（`WebKitNetworkProcess` 起不来 → 进程 `code=-1`）。
> 自 v5.1.5 起 AppImage 已注入 glib 隔离修复（断开包内旧 glib 与系统新 gio 模块的混用），但**尚未在
> 24.04 真机上逐一验证**，稳妥起见仍建议优先 `.deb`：`sudo apt install ./AICoder_6.6.0_amd64.deb` 自动解依赖。

### 移动端伴侣 · v0.9.2

> Android 侧载分发，需要在系统设置中允许「未知来源安装」。iOS 暂未发布。
> 移动端版本号与桌面端独立维护：移动端 v0.9.2。

| 平台 | 下载链接 | 用途 |
|------|---------|------|
| Android APK | [AICoder-mobile-v0.9.2.apk](https://pub-9d9e6c0cb6934fb0a0c505e3c64f39b2.r2.dev/aicoder-mobile/releases/mobile-v0.9.2/AICoder-mobile-v0.9.2.apk) | 用户直接安装 |
| Android AAB | [AICoder-mobile-v0.9.2.aab](https://pub-9d9e6c0cb6934fb0a0c505e3c64f39b2.r2.dev/aicoder-mobile/releases/mobile-v0.9.2/AICoder-mobile-v0.9.2.aab) | Google Play 上架用（暂存档） |

**v0.9.2 — 额度快用完时先确认**：Claude 额度到守卫线时，新建会话、继续发消息前先问一句（需桌面端 v6.2.1）。v0.9.1 起历史为空时会说明原因，拉取失败不再清空已显示的历史；v0.9.0 起手机上看得到 Codex 的历史与工具调用过程，详见 [移动端版本历史](#移动端版本历史)。

**🔐 签名提示**：v0.3.5 之前所有版本都是 CI 临时 debug 签名，与 v0.3.6+ 的稳定 release keystore 不一致——
**仍在 v0.1.0 ~ v0.3.5 的用户首次升级到 v0.4.0 必须卸载旧版重装一次**（一次性）；v0.3.6 及之后的用户可直接 OTA 覆盖升级，不受影响。

### 安装步骤

1. 下载上方安装包
2. 双击运行安装程序
3. 选择安装语言（中文/英文）
4. 按提示完成安装
5. 启动应用，开始使用

### macOS 安全提示

首次打开应用时，macOS 可能会提示「无法验证开发者」，或在 Apple Silicon 上提示「已损坏，无法打开，你应该将它移到废纸篓」。

这是因为应用走 ad-hoc 签名、未经 Apple 公证（Notarization），**并非恶意软件**。请打开「终端」执行以下命令解除限制，再重新打开应用：

```bash
sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/智码 AICoder.app"
```

输入 Mac 登录密码后即可正常打开应用。若没把应用拖进 Applications，可把 `.app` 直接拖进终端窗口自动补全路径。

## 更新机制

应用内置自动更新功能：

- 启动后自动检查更新（首次延迟 5 秒，之后每 30 分钟检查一次）
- 发现新版本后，右上角浮动通知显示「有可用更新」
- 点击「立即更新」按钮，自动下载并安装
- 安装完成后自动重启应用

更新清单文件: [update.json](update.json)

## 移动端版本历史

### mobile-v0.9.2 (2026-10-08)

手机端额度守卫：Claude 额度快用完时，新建会话和继续发消息前先确认：

**新功能**

- **新建会话前先确认额度** — Claude 账号额度到守卫线时，手机上新建会话会先弹出确认，文案由桌面按套餐和重置时刻给出，确认后才创建
- **会话里继续发消息前先确认** — 额度到线时同样先问一句，取消则输入框里的内容原样保留；会话的第一句不问（新建时已经问过）

**说明**

- 需要桌面端 v6.2.1 及以上；桌面端是旧版时不弹确认，照常发送

### mobile-v0.9.1 (2026-10-06)

历史记录显示更稳、「关于」页信息更正：

**问题修复**

- **会话历史为空时说明原因** — 桌面端版本过旧、还没关联上 CLI 的会话记录、CLI 还没写下记录、远程主机上的会话暂不支持、读取失败等各有提示，不再只显示「暂无历史消息」
- **拉取历史失败不再清空** — 网络抖一下时保留已显示的历史，不再整页清成「暂无历史消息」
- **实时终端只保留最近一段输出** — 跑得久的会话打开也不卡
- **「关于」页信息更正** — 显示安装包的真实版本号（此前一直显示 v0.1），去掉了错误的「MIT License」字样

### mobile-v0.9.0 (2026-10-04)

手机上看得到 Codex 的历史与工具调用过程，认得出 CLI 停在登录页：

**新功能**

- **一次回复一张卡** — 原来一个回复按消息拆成好几张卡，每张一个头像；现在一轮回复一张卡，Codex 的工具调用过程（如 `Called codex.list_mcp_resources(...)`）也显示出来，回答中展开、答完自动折叠
- **读得到 Codex 会话的历史** — 原来 Codex 会话在手机上永远「暂无历史消息」，只能看原始终端流；终端模式与聊天模式都已支持
- **认得出 CLI 停在登录页** — 没登录的 CLI 停在浏览器授权页时手机上会提示（这一页没有输入框，发进去的字会被吞），发消息前先拦一下

**问题修复**

- **「中断」只在回答中出现** — 没东西可停时不再挂着，点了也不再报「桌面端处理出错」
- **终端流平时收起来** — 有历史时回复卡已经带回答和工具过程，终端流收进快捷条「终端」按钮，只在读不到历史时兜底显示；往上翻历史不再被一直拽回底部
- **页面重载后顶部钻到状态栏底下** — 记下系统注入的状态栏边距，重载后先补上

**说明**

- 前三项新功能需要桌面端 v6.1.2 及以上
- 还在用 v0.7.0 的请先卸载再装（v0.7.0 误用了临时调试签名，覆盖安装会失败；卸载后需重新配对桌面）；其他版本可直接覆盖升级

### mobile-v0.8.0 (2026-09-30)

AI 回复完成时可以响一声提示音了：

**新功能**

- **回复完成提示音** — 「我的 → 通知」新增开关、音色、音量和试听；8 种音色与电脑端是同一套合成音（叮咚 / 钟声 / 成功音 / 闹铃 / 气泡 / 水晶 / 梦幻 / 水滴）。默认关闭：走手机媒体音量，静音 / 勿扰模式下同样会响
- **在对话页也响** — 最常见的用法就是开着对话页、手机放一边等它答完；顶部横幅则只在你正看着那个会话时不弹，看着别的会话照弹（原来在任何对话页都不弹）

**问题修复**

- **聊天模式会话一直显示「未连上终端」** — 聊天模式在桌面上不开终端，状态条原来只看终端；现在读桌面上报的运行态，显示「聊天模式 · 已连上桌面 / 正在回复…」，回复结束立刻刷新历史。需桌面端 v6.1.0 及以上

**说明**

- 桌面端下一版起，手机的「回复完成」改用桌面的判定（与电脑端提示音同一个）：报错的一轮、没有回答的一轮不算，聊天模式的会话也会提醒。连 v6.1.0 及更早的桌面端时，仍按终端输出停够几秒来判断
- 提示音与横幅都只保证 App 在前台时生效
- **还在用 v0.7.0 的请先卸载再装** — v0.7.0 当时误用了临时调试签名出包，与之前、之后各版的正式签名不一致，覆盖安装会被系统拒绝。卸载会清掉已配对的桌面，装好后重新配对即可；v0.7.1 及其他版本可直接覆盖升级

### mobile-v0.7.1 (2026-09-17)

手机能给聊天模式会话发消息了：

- **聊天模式会话此前在手机上只能转圈到超时** — 它们永远没有 PTY，而手机端原来只认 PTY 那条路
- **现已走独立通道** — 手机发出的消息直达聊天会话，回答同样回流到手机
- **需配套桌面端 v5.9.0** — 改动落在 H5 与远程服务端各一半，两边须同版本

### mobile-v0.7.0 (2026-09-14)

### mobile-v0.3.6 (2026-05-08)

- **🔐 关键修复：固定生产签名 keystore（一次性破坏升级）**
  - **根因**：v0.3.5 之前 CI 仓库未配置 `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` secret，每次构建用 GitHub runner 临时生成的 debug.keystore 签名 → 每个版本签名指纹都不同 → 用户每次升级都报"签名不一致"必须卸载重装
  - **修复**：本地生成稳定的生产 RSA 4096 keystore（SHA-256: `A5:B6:4A:F5:33:...:6B:02:BA`，有效期 100 年），配置到 CI 仓库 secrets，从 v0.3.6 开始所有版本都用同一 keystore 签名
  - **影响**：
    - 旧版（v0.1.0 ~ v0.3.5）用户**必须卸载后重装 v0.3.6**（一次性）
    - 装上 v0.3.6 后，未来所有版本（v0.3.7、v0.4.x...）都可直接 OTA 覆盖升级，不再卸载

- v0.3.5 中间版本因仍用 debug 签名实际未发布到下载源

守护进程方案 — 主进程崩溃自动重启 + 会话自动恢复 + CLI 输出不中断：

- **守护进程架构（A-Enhanced）** — 引入 watchdog + pty-host 双 sidecar 进程：watchdog 监控主进程崩溃自动重启；pty-host 独立持有 PTY master，CLI 子进程不受主进程崩溃影响，继续运行
- **会话自动恢复** — 主进程崩溃 / 用户结束进程后，watchdog 自动重启主进程，所有活跃会话标签自动恢复，CLI 输出继续流式刷新（token 不浪费、对话不中断）
- **MessagePack RPC + 环形缓冲** — 前后端通过 named pipe / UDS + MessagePack 通信，每会话 2 MiB 环形缓冲保证重连无缝接续历史输出
- **AICODER_SUPERVISED 防 fork bomb 守卫** — 自重生路径加 env 守卫；watchdog 退出时主动清理 pty-host 子进程，避免僵尸进程
- **静默后台运行** — sidecar binary 用 GUI subsystem + CREATE_NO_WINDOW 标志，无任何命令行黑窗

WebView2 崩溃自愈 + 内存预防 + 多项关键修复：

### v3.6.0 (2026-05-14)

本次更新带来更清晰的产品体验：

- **设置-关于页新增产品说明区域** — 随时查看产品边界与商标信息
- **Provider 选项命名优化** — 措辞更直观清晰
- **终端性能提升** — TUI 会话消息加载更快、会话标题显示更稳定
- **无感升级** — 旧版配置自动适配新结构,本地数据无需手动操作

## 项目结构

```
aicoder-release/
├── README.md           # 本文件
├── update.json         # 桌面端自动更新清单（Tauri Updater 读取）
├── .gitignore          # Git 忽略规则
├── screenshots/        # README 里的应用预览图
└── releases-mobile/    # 移动端伴侣 Android APK + AAB（独立版本号）
    └── mobile-vX.Y.Z/  # 每版含 universal-release APK + AAB
```

> **桌面端产物不在仓库里**（自 v5.8.3 起）。每版 12 个文件改放
> [Releases 附件](https://github.com/bkywksj/aicoder-release/releases)，
> 因为仓库 blob 有两条硬约束：单文件 100 MiB 上限（AppImage 已 93 MB），
> 以及 58 个版本把仓库顶到 10 GB。Releases 附件不计入仓库配额、单文件上限 2 GB。
>
> 下载与自动更新都不受影响：主源是 R2 CDN，备源是本仓 Releases 附件。
> Gitee 仓只作存档（大文件需登录才能下载），不在应用内下载源里。
> 历史版本的完整归档在 R2（`releases/vX.Y.Z/`，比本仓曾经存过的更全）。

## 发布新版本流程

1. 在主项目中更新版本号（`tauri.conf.json` / `Cargo.toml` / `package.json`）
2. 打 Git Tag（`v*.*.*` 格式）并推送到 GitHub，CI 自动构建 Windows + macOS 安装包
3. 从 GitHub Release 下载产物，本地推送到本仓库并生成 `update.json`

# 智码 AICoder

> 一站式 AI 编程助手管理平台 — 支持 Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI

## 简介

智码 AICoder 是一款轻量级桌面应用，为 AI CLI 编程工具打造统一管理平台。支持 **Claude Code**、**Codex CLI**、**Gemini CLI** 三大 AI 编程助手，提供可视化的会话管理、多标签终端、Token 统计和开发效率工具，让你在一个桌面应用中高效管理所有 AI 编程工作流。

## 应用预览

### 主界面 — 多项目会话管理 + 快捷键面板

## 核心功能

- **多工具统一管理** — 支持 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Gemini CLI，自动检测已安装工具和版本，一键切换
- **终端管理** — 内置 PTY 终端，支持多标签页并行会话，会话可弹出为独立窗口
- **会话管理** — 创建、切换、收藏会话，按项目自动分组，8 种颜色标记，模糊搜索秒找历史对话
- **多账号隔离** — 多实例完全独立（登录凭据/API Key/会话记录/配置），支持同时使用公司和个人账号
- **Claude 会话浏览** — 查看历史对话记录，支持搜索和导出（Markdown/HTML），自动生成会话摘要
- **Token 统计** — 实时追踪 API 用量（输入/输出/缓存分别统计），每日趋势图 + 月度总览 + 180 天热力图
- **代码片段** — 保存常用 Prompt 和代码模板，支持模板变量，一键插入终端
- **AI 记忆管理** — 支持多 AI 提供商的记忆生成和管理
- **快捷命令面板** — `Ctrl+K` 整合内置指令、项目命令、代码片段，智能排序
- **内置浏览器** — 分屏预览网页应用
- **文件浏览器** — 树形浏览项目文件，20+ 种文件类型图标
- **Git 面板** — 查看当前分支、提交日志、文件变更状态
- **API 配置管理** — 多 API Profile 切换，支持不同密钥和端点配置
- **MCP Server 管理** — 可视化管理 Model Context Protocol 服务器配置
- **CLAUDE.md 编辑器** — 项目级和全局 CLAUDE.md 在线编辑
- **深色/浅色主题** — 跟随系统或手动切换，护眼舒适
- **系统托盘** — 最小化到托盘，常驻后台
- **自动更新** — 内置 OTA 更新，新版本自动推送
- **零额外开销** — CLI 原生运行，不拦截/不修改/不转发 API 请求，费用与直接用终端完全一样

- **操作系统**: Windows 10/11 (x64)、macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel)
- **运行时**: 无需额外安装（Windows WebView2 已内置于 Windows 10+）
- **磁盘**: ~10 MB 安装空间

### macOS 安全提示

首次打开应用时，macOS 可能会提示「无法验证开发者」，或在 Apple Silicon 上提示「已损坏，无法打开，你应该将它移到废纸篓」。

这是因为应用走 ad-hoc 签名、未经 Apple 公证（Notarization），**并非恶意软件**。请打开「终端」执行以下命令解除限制，再重新打开应用：

```bash
sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/智码 AICoder.app"
```

输入 Mac 登录密码后即可正常打开应用。若没把应用拖进 Applications，可把 `.app` 直接拖进终端窗口自动补全路径。

## 更新机制

应用内置自动更新功能：

- 启动后自动检查更新（首次延迟 5 秒，之后每 30 分钟检查一次）
- 发现新版本后，右上角浮动通知显示「有可用更新」
- 点击「立即更新」按钮，自动下载并安装
- 安装完成后自动重启应用

更新清单文件: [update.json](update.json)

- **额度打满后自动换下一个档案接着跑** — 一个 token 的额度打满，此前要手动去设置里切档案、再回终端点「继续」；跑长任务时这一步经常发生在人不在场的时候，任务就一直卡着。现在自动完成：冷却当前档案 → 选下一个 → 探活 → 静默切换 → 重启会话 → 续发原提示词

- **预防式提前切换真正接上用量数据** — 此前只有开关和阈值、触发逻辑没写（界面上有、实际不工作）。现在读 Codex 的 rate_limits 与 Grok 的配额，在额度接近上限时切换；且**只在一轮回答刚结束、会话回到空闲的那一刻动手**，不打断正在跑的任务
- **冷却状态落库** — 限额窗口常达 5 小时甚至一周，只存内存的话重启应用就忘了，一上来又撞回同一个已耗尽的档案

### v5.1.6 (2026-08-24)

远程 SSH 稳定性与多 Agent 编排唤醒修复：

**🔌 远程 SSH**

- **用着用着就断，且只能重启客户端才好** — 报错 `channel_open_session 失败 (ConnectFailed)` 不是断网，是服务端 sshd 的会话槽位（MaxSessions，默认 10）被耗尽。两个根因：看门狗探测开完通道直接丢弃、不发关闭帧，sshd 对这种「开了没执行」的通道永不回收，约 7 分钟漏光；连接复用时一次都不验活，废连接被无限复用 —— 于是「点连接提示成功、紧接着的探测就报错，怎么点都好不了」
- **同一主机的多条命令不再互相阻塞** — 开通道不再把连接锁一路持到命令跑完，单条卡死也不会拖垮整台主机
