          tests/integration/test_marked_rollup_migration_native.py
          tests/integration/test_marked_durable_folds_native.py
          tests/integration/test_marked_sql_surface_native.py
      - name: pytest online-index durability on a private physical standby
        timeout-minutes: 8
        env:
          LOOM_PG_IMAGE: postgres:${{ matrix.postgres }}
          LOOM_PG_CONTAINER: loom-scale-index-drill-pg
          LOOM_PG_HOST_PORT: "15432"
          LOOM_PG_INDEX_DRILL: "1"
          LOOM_PG_INDEX_DRILL_DSN: postgres://loom:loomdev@localhost:15432/loom
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for name in loom-scale-index-drill-pg loom-scale-index-drill-pg-standby; do
            if docker container inspect "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "drill container already exists: $name" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          if docker network inspect loom-scale-index-drill-pg-net >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "drill network already exists" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          cleanup() {
            docker rm -f -v loom-scale-index-drill-pg loom-scale-index-drill-pg-standby || true
            docker network rm loom-scale-index-drill-pg-net || true

          trap cleanup EXIT
          bash dev/ci_start_postgres.sh
          docker update --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g loom-scale-index-drill-pg loom-scale-index-drill-pg-standby
          pytest -q tests/integration/test_pg_online_index_durability.py
      - name: pytest placement durability on a private physical standby
        timeout-minutes: 8
        env:
          LOOM_PG_IMAGE: postgres:${{ matrix.postgres }}
          LOOM_PG_CONTAINER: loom-scale-place-drill-pg
          LOOM_PG_HOST_PORT: "0"
          LOOM_CELL_PLACE_DRILL: "1"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for name in loom-scale-place-drill-pg loom-scale-place-drill-pg-standby; do
            if docker container inspect "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "drill container already exists: $name" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          if docker network inspect loom-scale-place-drill-pg-net >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "drill network already exists" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          cleanup() {
            docker rm -f -v loom-scale-place-drill-pg loom-scale-place-drill-pg-standby || true
            docker network rm loom-scale-place-drill-pg-net || true
          }
          trap cleanup EXIT
          bash dev/ci_start_postgres.sh
          # Docker reserves the host port; use only this primary's loopback mapping.

            exit 1
          fi
          port=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
          if (( port > 65535 )); then
            echo "invalid placement drill loopback mapping" >&2
            exit 1

      # The tenant-isolation gates again, against a second server that enforces auth:
      # the Postgres read paths (heads by key and by id, narrowed scopes) see real tokens.
      # They run whether or not the memory suites passed (`!cancelled()`).
      - name: Boot control plane with auth on
        id: auth_on
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.issuer.outcome == 'success' }}
        env:
          LOOM_AUTH_REQUIRED: "true"
          LOOM_INSTANCE_LABEL: "ci:integration-postgres-auth"
          LOOM_CH_ANALYSIS_PROBE_INTERVAL_S: "10"
        run: |
          LOOM_WEB_WORKERS=3 PORT=7778 nohup sh scripts/serve.sh > server-auth.log 2>&1 &
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            curl -fsS http://localhost:7778/v1/health && exit 0
            sleep 1
          done
          echo "auth-on control plane never became healthy"
          tail -100 server-auth.log
          exit 1
      # The isolation files that write or read memory. Two read-scope tests seed
      # superseded and duplicate rows by writing ClickHouse directly, rows the Postgres
      # authority never held, and the isolation part's other files (run claims, the
      # extraction queue, projection failures) hold no Postgres row: they run on the
      # ClickHouse job.
      - name: pytest isolation gates (Postgres authority, auth on)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.auth_on.outcome == 'success' }}
        env:
          LOOM_AUTH_REQUIRED: "true"
          LOOM_BASE_URL: http://localhost:7778
          LOOM_CH_ANALYSIS_PROBE_INTERVAL_S: "10"
        run: >-
          pytest -q
          tests/integration/test_cross_principal_leakage.py
          tests/integration/test_read_scope_isolation.py
          tests/integration/test_session_briefs.py
          tests/integration/test_token_mint.py
          tests/integration/_sdk_handoff_ci.py
          tests/integration/test_mcp_session_run_scope.py
          tests/integration/test_onboard_tenant.py
          tests/integration/test_blacklist.py
          tests/integration/test_mirror_checked_search_http.py
          tests/integration/test_mirror_checked_list_http.py
          tests/integration/test_analysis_isolation.py
          tests/integration/test_sensitivity_high_canary.py
          tests/integration/test_pg_authority.py
          -k "not test_a_duplicate_never_resolves_to_a_canonical_outside_the_scope
          and not test_a_superseded_hit_never_names_a_successor_outside_the_scope"
      # Last, on its own: `loom reconcile` acts on the whole database, every other test's
      # rows included, so it runs after them all and in its file's order.
      - name: pytest (loom reconcile drills)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/integration/test_restore_reconcile.py
      - name: Upload server log on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: server-log-postgres-${{ matrix.postgres }}
          path: |
            server.log
            server-auth.log

  mixed-version:
    needs: [validate-ref, clickhouse]
    name: builds N-1 and N on one ClickHouse
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      LOOM_CLICKHOUSE_IMAGE: ${{ needs.clickhouse.outputs.image }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # The gate builds each build's dashboard bundle.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        id: python
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: uv.lock
      - name: Install Loom from uv.lock
        run: |
          uv sync --locked --python "${{ steps.python.outputs.python-path }}" --extra dev --extra code
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      # The base is HEAD~1: the previous commit on a push, and on a pull request the
      # first parent of its merge commit, the target branch as the merge was made. The
      # target branch's tip can carry a newer migration by the time the run starts.
      - name: Mixed-version gate
        run: python scripts/gates/mixed_version.py --require --base HEAD~1
      - name: Published build ordinary-event compatibility
        run: python scripts/gates/mixed_version.py --require --base 1cbaf0411114512957b96ec5ea7bbb8058828543

  sdk-rust:
    needs: validate-ref
    name: rust sdk (${{ matrix.rust }}, fmt, tests, clippy, docs, package)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        rust: ["1.84.1", stable]
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: sdk/rust
    env:
      CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_RUST_VERSIONS: fallback
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install Rust with format and lint components
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install "${{ matrix.rust }}" --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
          rustup override set "${{ matrix.rust }}"
      # The library leaves dependency locking to its consumers; each toolchain resolves once.
      - name: Resolve dependencies for this toolchain
        run: cargo generate-lockfile
      - name: Rust formatting
        run: cargo fmt --check
      - name: Unit, HTTP contract and documentation tests
        run: cargo test --locked
      - name: Lint the library, tests and examples
        run: cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: API documentation
        env:
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings
        run: cargo doc --locked --no-deps
      - name: Verify the distributable crate and its license
        run: |
          cargo package --locked
          for archive in target/package/clickhouse-loom-*.crate; do
            package="$(basename "$archive" .crate)"
            tar -xOf "$archive" "$package/LICENSE" | cmp - ../../LICENSE
          done

  sdk-typescript:
    needs: validate-ref
    name: typescript sdk (generated types in sync, lint, tsc, vitest, dist)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        id: python
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: uv.lock
      - name: Install Loom from uv.lock (no extras)
        run: |
          uv sync --locked --python "${{ steps.python.outputs.python-path }}"
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      # The SDK's operation table and wire types are generated from the
      # server's registry; a server change that alters a
      # request or response shape must regenerate them in the same PR.
      - name: generated ops.ts is current
        run: python scripts/codegen/sdk_ts_gen.py --check
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: sdk/typescript/package-lock.json
      - name: npm ci
        working-directory: sdk/typescript
        run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
      # biome lint + format, tsc --noEmit, version consistency, the README's
      # ts examples type-checked against src, vitest.
      - name: lint + type-check + version + README examples + unit tests
        working-directory: sdk/typescript
        run: npm run check
      # ESM + CJS build, the dist tests over the exact export
      # list, publint and arethetypeswrong — the package must resolve for
      # CommonJS consumers and bundlers before it is ever published.
      - name: build + dist tests + publint + attw
        working-directory: sdk/typescript
        run: npm run check:dist
      # Keep the locked 1.8 baseline above and qualify the other supported band
      # against the same source, native tool runner and package exports.
      - name: Claude memory tool with Anthropic 1.11
        working-directory: sdk/typescript
        run: |
          npm install --no-save --package-lock=false --no-audit --no-fund @anthropic-ai/sdk@1.11.0
          npm run type-check
          npx vitest run src/integrations/claude-memory.test.ts src/integrations/claude-memory-runner.test.ts
          npx vitest run --config vitest.dist.config.ts test/package/exports.test.ts

  sdk-python-adapters:
    needs: validate-ref
    name: python sdk adapters (py ${{ matrix.python }}${{ matrix.lowest && ', lowest deps' || '' }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # The framework adapters' tests and types, each with the framework its SDK extra
    # names, in a venv of its own: their dependencies are not in uv.lock, and two
    # frameworks may pin one package incompatibly.
    # The lowest-deps leg installs every direct requirement (the SDK's own, the
    # extra's, pytest) at its lower bound.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - python: "3.12"
          - python: "3.11"
            lowest: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - name: Adapter tests and mypy --strict
        run: make test-sdk-adapters SDK_ADAPTERS_PYTHON="$(which python)" SDK_ADAPTERS_RESOLUTION="${{ matrix.lowest && 'lowest-direct' || 'highest' }}"

  sdk-python-package:
    needs: validate-ref
    name: python sdk wheel (py ${{ matrix.python }}${{ matrix.lowest && ', lowest deps' || '' }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every other job runs the SDK inside the server's 3.12 environment, whose
    # dependencies and interpreter hide what a clean install on the SDK's floor
    # lacks. This one installs the built wheel alone, with only its declared
    # deps, on the floor and the newest Python; the lowest-deps legs pin each
    # declared dep to its lower bound.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - python: "3.11"
          - python: "3.12"
          - python: "3.14"
          - python: "3.11"
            lowest: true
          - python: "3.14"
            lowest: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - name: Install uv
        run: pip install uv
      - name: Build wheel + sdist
        run: uv build sdk/python --out-dir dist
      - name: Install the wheel into a clean venv
        env:
          RESOLUTION: ${{ matrix.lowest && 'lowest-direct' || 'highest' }}
        run: |
          WHEEL=$(ls dist/*.whl)
          uv venv --python "$(which python)" /tmp/sdk-venv
          # The wheel's Requires-Dist lines, passed as direct requirements so
          # lowest-direct lowers them (a wheel's own deps count as transitive).
          unzip -p "$WHEEL" '*.dist-info/METADATA' | sed -n 's/^Requires-Dist: //p' > /tmp/sdk-deps.txt
          uv pip install --python /tmp/sdk-venv/bin/python --resolution "$RESOLUTION" \
            "$WHEEL" -r /tmp/sdk-deps.txt
          uv pip list --python /tmp/sdk-venv/bin/python
      - name: Smoke-test the installed wheel
        run: /tmp/sdk-venv/bin/python scripts/gates/sdk_wheel_smoke.py dist/*.whl

  langflow-extension:
    needs: validate-ref
    name: Langflow extension wheel (py ${{ matrix.python }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python: ["3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - name: Build the SDK and extension distributions
        run: |
          uv build sdk/python --out-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-sdk-dist"
          uv build integrations/langflow --out-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-extension-dist"
          mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-sdist"
          tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP"/langflow-extension-dist/*.tar.gz -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-sdist"
          uv build "$RUNNER_TEMP"/langflow-sdist/* --wheel --out-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-rebuilt-dist"
      - name: Install and discover the extension outside the checkout
        run: |
          uv venv --python "$(command -v python)" "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-extension-venv"
          uv pip install --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-extension-venv/bin/python" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP"/langflow-sdk-dist/*.whl \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP"/langflow-rebuilt-dist/*.whl "lfx==1.13.3"
          uv pip check --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-extension-venv/bin/python"
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          env -u PYTHONPATH "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-extension-venv/bin/python" -I \
            "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/gates/langflow_extension_smoke.py" \
            "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-extension-dist" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-rebuilt-dist" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/langflow-sdk-dist"
sampled_files.Dockerfile:
# Loom Control Plane production image.
#
# Builder stages, then the runtime (docs/operations/deployment.md lists each). uvicorn
# binds via the container's PORT env var.

# Base images are pinned by digest; Renovate (renovate.json) keeps the pins current.
FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:a6e34c598f2467ed0e9a8d349809fcd8b5c603269512df273a0bb1784edc11b1 AS py-builder
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.2@sha256:069a51314a7bb6031777a9273205fe1b0b19e914ef418207d1338b268df641dd /uv /bin/uv
WORKDIR /build
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock README.md ./
COPY server ./server
COPY sdk ./sdk
# [lemma] (lemmagen3) ships in the image: it is the lexical leg's English
# lemmatizer and needs build-essential to compile, which is why it is an
# extra rather than a core dep (a host that only runs the `loom` CLI must
# `pip install -e .` without a compiler).
# [aws] (boto3) ships in the image for `loom export-analytics` and for
# LOOM_DOCUMENT_OBJECT_STORE=s3 (document originals in a bucket).
# [code] extras (tree-sitter, numpy) ship in the image: the code-plane
# workers and the async code.refresh path lazy-import them at runtime,
# so a plain "." install boots green and then crashes on first ingest.
# [local-embedder] (fastembed plus onnxruntime) ships in the image: the
# released stack embeds with it, and the runtime stage carries its default
# model's pinned files, so a stack started with no network still embeds.
# Dependencies come from uv.lock exactly (--locked: the build fails when the
# lock no longer matches pyproject.toml; hashes checked) into a venv the
# runtime stage copies at the same path.
ENV UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy
RUN uv sync --locked --no-editable --no-cache \
    --extra aws --extra code --extra lemma --extra local-embedder

# The default local embedding model, at its pinned revision and checked by sha256
# (server/embedding/local_models.py), in a stage keyed on the venv and server/ alone,
# so a frontend or docs change does not fetch it again.
FROM py-builder AS local-models
RUN LOOM_LOCAL_EMBEDDING_MODEL_DIR=/models /opt/venv/bin/python -m server.embedding.local_models fetch bge-small

FROM node:22-alpine@sha256:0a7108bf6c7bf5de370ffb1a3ed6be93d405b43ff159f681a8d18c0e2bc2e402 AS frontend-builder
WORKDIR /frontend
COPY frontend/package.json frontend/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY frontend/ ./
COPY scripts/release/frontend_third_party_notices.mjs /tmp/loom-license/
COPY scripts/release/license_fallbacks /tmp/loom-license/license_fallbacks
RUN node /tmp/loom-license/frontend_third_party_notices.mjs --root /frontend \
    --output /frontend/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt \
    && npm run build \
    && cp /frontend/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt /frontend/dist/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt

# The Go toolchain and scip-go for the Go compiler-tier worker
# (code_scip_go_delta), built here so the runtime stage copies a finished
# /usr/local/go and one binary. Pinned; TARGETARCH picks the tarball (amd64 or
# arm64), checked against the sha256 go.dev publishes for it (a new GO_VERSION
# needs its two checksums too). scip-go's module download is verified by the Go
# checksum database.
FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:a6e34c598f2467ed0e9a8d349809fcd8b5c603269512df273a0bb1784edc11b1 AS go-builder
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG GO_VERSION=1.27.3
ARG GO_SHA256_AMD64=65efbc80fdc1fa2cd2631cad5b481777a68e8725f34e89f50fc6ac714e379b40
ARG GO_SHA256_ARM64=a06e99309dbcbdca1a8ccd2282c3ee146e55930886e26b4f1193269587165f49
ARG SCIP_GO_VERSION=v0.2.7
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && case "${TARGETARCH:-amd64}" in \
         amd64) GO_SHA256="${GO_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
         arm64) GO_SHA256="${GO_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
         *) echo "no pinned Go tarball for ${TARGETARCH}" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
       esac \
    && curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 20 --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3 "https://go.dev/dl/go${GO_VERSION}.linux-${TARGETARCH:-amd64}.tar.gz" -o /tmp/go.tgz \
    && printf '%s  /tmp/go.tgz\n' "${GO_SHA256}" >/tmp/go.tgz.sha256 \
    && sha256sum -c /tmp/go.tgz.sha256 \
    && tar -C /usr/local -xzf /tmp/go.tgz && rm /tmp/go.tgz /tmp/go.tgz.sha256
ENV PATH=/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH GOPATH=/go GOFLAGS=-mod=mod
RUN go install "github.com/scip-code/scip-go/cmd/scip-go@${SCIP_GO_VERSION}" \
    && cp /go/bin/scip-go /usr/local/bin/scip-go

# Node and scip-typescript for the
# TypeScript compiler-tier worker (code_scip_ts_delta), fetched the way the Go
# stage fetches Go — the official glibc tarball, pinned, TARGETARCH picks it —
# with compiler indexers and package managers installed into one prefix so the
# runtime stage can prepare fresh checkouts automatically. The tarball is
# checked against the sha256 in the release's
# SHASUMS256.txt (a new NODE_VERSION needs its two checksums too).
FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:a6e34c598f2467ed0e9a8d349809fcd8b5c603269512df273a0bb1784edc11b1 AS node-builder
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG NODE_VERSION=22.23.4
ARG NODE_SHA256_X64=1805bcd35e6815559bd2eb97db438d3fdb0eb3a5e6a977b7c1badca76337e9ce
ARG NODE_SHA256_ARM64=6287aa46b6c375d816e63ae66d024fbbfd70404825aabdfdf898a970871d2f4b
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl xz-utils \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && case "${TARGETARCH:-amd64}" in \
         amd64) NODE_ARCH=x64 NODE_SHA256="${NODE_SHA256_X64}" ;; \
         arm64) NODE_ARCH=arm64 NODE_SHA256="${NODE_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
         *) echo "no pinned Node tarball for ${TARGETARCH}" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
       esac \
    && curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 20 --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3 "https://nodejs.org/dist/v${NODE_VERSION}/node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz" -o /tmp/node.txz \
    && printf '%s  /tmp/node.txz\n' "${NODE_SHA256}" >/tmp/node.txz.sha256 \
    && sha256sum -c /tmp/node.txz.sha256 \
    && mkdir -p /usr/local/node && tar -C /usr/local/node --strip-components=1 -xJf /tmp/node.txz && rm /tmp/node.txz /tmp/node.txz.sha256
ENV PATH=/usr/local/node/bin:$PATH
COPY scripts/install-code-toolchains.sh /tmp/install-code-toolchains.sh
COPY scripts/code-toolchains /tmp/code-toolchains
RUN LOOM_CODE_TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX=/usr/local/node sh /tmp/install-code-toolchains.sh \
    && npm cache clean --force

# The C++ compiler tier (code_scip_delta, code_scip_full). scip-clang ships an
# x86_64 Linux binary only, so the image carries it on amd64; elsewhere point
# LOOM_CODE_SCIP_CLANG_PATH at your own build. The keyring holds the pinned LLVM
# signing key alone: the runtime stage installs clang, lld and the llvm tools a
# repository's CMake configure looks for (it writes the compile_commands.json
# scip-clang reads).
FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:a6e34c598f2467ed0e9a8d349809fcd8b5c603269512df273a0bb1784edc11b1 AS cpp-builder
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG SCIP_CLANG_VERSION=v0.4.0
ARG SCIP_CLANG_SHA256_AMD64=06fd18c576f979a726c651594644ec4a35db4f471f2160b3f72eb89fa6001784
ARG LLVM_SIGNER_FPR=6084F3CF814B57C1CF12EFD515CF4D18AF4F7421
# Downloads retry a briefly unreachable host; the key goes to a file so a retry never
# feeds gpg a repeated partial stream.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl gnupg \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && mkdir -p /out/bin \
    && export GNUPGHOME="$(mktemp -d)" \
    && curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 20 --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3 https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key -o /tmp/llvm.key \
    && gpg --batch --import /tmp/llvm.key \
    && gpg --batch --export "${LLVM_SIGNER_FPR}" >/out/llvm.gpg \
    && [ "$(gpg --show-keys --with-colons /out/llvm.gpg | grep -c '^pub:')" = 1 ] \
    && gpg --show-keys --with-colons /out/llvm.gpg | grep -q "^fpr:::::::::${LLVM_SIGNER_FPR}:" \
    && if [ "${TARGETARCH:-amd64}" = amd64 ]; then \
         curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 20 --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3 "https://github.com/sourcegraph/scip-clang/releases/download/${SCIP_CLANG_VERSION}/scip-clang-x86_64-linux" -o /out/bin/scip-clang \
         && printf '%s  /out/bin/scip-clang\n' "${SCIP_CLANG_SHA256_AMD64}" | sha256sum -c \
         && chmod 0755 /out/bin/scip-clang; \
       fi

FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:a6e34c598f2467ed0e9a8d349809fcd8b5c603269512df273a0bb1784edc11b1
# git: the code_ingest worker and async code.refresh maintain the bare
# repo mirror (fetch + cat-file) by shelling out to git. Mounted repos are
# owned by the host operator, not uid 999 — without safe.directory git
# refuses every command with "dubious ownership".
# bubblewrap: the repository-job sandbox (clone, fetch, dependency installs and
# the compiler tiers run inside it). It needs user namespaces, which Docker's
# default seccomp profile blocks: see "Repository-job sandbox" in
# docs/operations/code-index-operations.md for the container options.
# clang 21, lld, the llvm tools, cmake and ninja: the C++ tier's CMake configure
# (plain http: apt checks the signature against the pinned key).
COPY --from=cpp-builder /out/llvm.gpg /usr/share/keyrings/llvm.gpg
RUN echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/llvm.gpg] http://apt.llvm.org/trixie/ llvm-toolchain-trixie-21 main" \
      >/etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm.list \
    && apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    bubblewrap \
    ca-certificates \
    clang-21 \
    cmake \
    git \
    lld-21 \
    llvm-21 \
    ninja-build \
    xz-utils \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && git config --system safe.directory '*'
COPY --from=cpp-builder /out/bin/ /usr/local/bin/
WORKDIR /app
# Deployed commit, stamped in at build time and surfaced in /v1/health. Placed
# after the dependency layers so re-stamping a new commit doesn't bust the
# pip/npm caches. Defaults to "" (source runs report build_commit="unknown").
ARG LOOM_BUILD_COMMIT=""
ENV LOOM_BUILD_COMMIT=${LOOM_BUILD_COMMIT}
COPY LICENSE NOTICE THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES ./
COPY --from=py-builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
# `go` + scip-go on PATH so code_scip_go_delta can run in the
# workers container (a repository's Go compiler tier refreshes per merge)
COPY --from=go-builder /usr/local/go /usr/local/go
COPY --from=go-builder /usr/local/bin/scip-go /usr/local/bin/scip-go
# node, scip-typescript and pnpm on PATH
# so code_scip_ts_delta can run in the workers container (a repository's
# TypeScript compiler tier refreshes per merge instead of by a host-side run)
COPY --from=node-builder /usr/local/node /usr/local/node
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:/usr/local/node/bin:/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOMODCACHE=/app/var/gomodcache GOCACHE=/app/var/gocache
COPY server ./server
COPY sdk ./sdk
# Schema migrations: the `/v1/admin/schema.status` endpoint reads these
# at runtime to compute expected-vs-present table drift. Without them
# the endpoint flags every existing table as "extra".
COPY schemas ./schemas
# The assistant's agent definition, which a boot seeds into the LibreChat beside it.
COPY integrations/librechat/agent.yaml ./integrations/librechat/agent.yaml
# The compiler-tier workers (code_scip_delta, code_scip_go_delta,
# code_scip_ts_delta, code_scip_py_delta) shell out to scripts/scip_harness/run_*.sh resolved
# relative to server/ — without this COPY every in-container pass reports the
# harness missing, whatever toolchain the image carries.
COPY scripts/scip_harness ./scripts/scip_harness
COPY scripts/serve.sh ./scripts/serve.sh
# code.calibrate reads its probe corpus from bench/fixtures at a path
# hard-coded relative to the handler — without this COPY the op 422s
# in-container ("probe corpus missing").
COPY bench/fixtures ./bench/fixtures
# mentor.guide serves the agent guide (SKILL.md, reference.md) from here.
COPY skills/loom ./skills/loom
# help.search and help.get read the documentation from here (its Markdown; the
# screenshots under docs/images/ stay out of the build context, .dockerignore).
COPY docs ./docs
# Dev tooling — loom_init.py, loom_ingest.py, verify_audit_chain.py, backup
# and restore. Migrations run in the server's startup lifespan; these ship for
# `docker exec` operational tasks (token mint, knowledge ingest, audit verification).
COPY dev ./dev
# Built React/Vite dashboard. Served at / (index.html) and /assets/*.
# If this layer is missing, dashboard pages return 503 — admin endpoints
# at /v1/admin/* stay reachable via curl regardless.
COPY --from=frontend-builder /frontend/dist ./frontend/dist

# Non-root runtime. uid/gid 999: the compose files mount /run/loom (the
# per-server runtime files) as a tmpfs owned by it.
RUN groupadd -r -g 999 loom && useradd -r -u 999 -g loom -d /app loom \
    && mkdir -p /app/var/code_repos /app/var/gomodcache /app/var/gocache /app/var/cron/locks \
    && chown -R loom:loom /app \
    && install -d -o loom -g loom -m 0700 /run/loom
USER loom

# LOOM_BIND_HOST is the address the port is published on, which the startup
# checks read; LOOM_LISTEN_HOST is the one the container listens on, all its
# interfaces. 0.0.0.0 = reachable by others, so it needs the safeguards in
# docs/operations/deployment.md ("Proxy and TLS"). A compose stack that
# publishes on loopback passes its LOOM_BIND_HOST through.
# PYTHONPATH: the `loom` command imports the same /app tree as the server,
# not the copy in the venv, which ships without schemas/.
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONPATH=/app \
    PORT=7777 \
    LOOM_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
    LOOM_LISTEN_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
    LOOM_LOCAL_EMBEDDING_MODEL_DIR=/app/models

# Outside /app/var, which a deployment may mount over (the Helm chart's cache volume).
COPY --from=local-models --chown=loom:loom /models /app/models

EXPOSE 7777
# Readiness, not liveness: healthy once the replica can serve (migrations, keys
# and warm-up loaded), unhealthy while it drains. The start period covers a
# boot that waits on another replica's migration lease. With LOOM_TLS_CERT_FILE in
# the container's environment the check uses HTTPS without verifying the
# certificate: it reads only the readiness answer of its own loopback port.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=5s --start-period=900s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -c "import os, ssl, sys, urllib.request; tls=bool(os.environ.get('LOOM_TLS_CERT_FILE')); r=urllib.request.urlopen(('https' if tls else 'http')+'://127.0.0.1:'+os.environ.get('PORT','7777')+'/v1/health/ready', timeout=3, context=ssl._create_unverified_context() if tls else None); sys.exit(0 if r.status==200 else 1)" || exit 1

# The web tier: scripts/serve.sh says how it starts and stops. On SIGTERM Loom
# answers not-ready for LOOM_SHUTDOWN_READY_DELAY_S (15 s) while it serves, uvicorn
# then waits at most LOOM_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_S (10 s) for in-flight requests, the
# lifespan drains take at most 40 s (server/boot.py SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_BUDGET_S), and
# participant retirement runs last: compose's stop_grace_period is 75 s.
CMD ["/app/scripts/serve.sh"]

sampled_files.README.md:
ClickHouse Loom

Shared memory, document search and code intelligence for AI agents.
For Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and your own agents.

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Português (Brasil) · Español

What Loom is for · Benchmarks · Get started · Capabilities · Integrations · Documentation

Loom is an open-source, self-hosted MCP server that gives your agents long-term, shared memory: what one agent learns in a session, the next agent or tool can find. In an authenticated team deployment, each agent uses a token scoped to namespaces and read or write roles. [Check shared memory and denied access](./docs/getting-started/connect-a-coding-agent.md#share-a-team-namespace-with-separate-credentials). Agents connect through MCP, HTTP, Python or TypeScript. Self-host with Docker or [on Kubernetes with the Helm chart](./docs/operations/kubernetes.md); agent context and index data live in [ClickHouse](./docs/use-cases/self-hosted-clickhouse.md), and a deployment can choose [Postgres at first boot](./docs/operations/postgres.md) for live memory and knowledge state. The dashboard brings memories, repositories, tasks and runs into one place. ## What Loom is for - **Long-term memory shared across your coding agents**, with plugins that load context at session start and capture the session as it runs. [Agent memory](./docs/use-cases/agent-memory.md) · [Connect a coding agent](./docs/getting-started/connect-a-coding-agent.md) - **Memory for an agent application**, per user, from the Python or TypeScript SDK. [Your first agent](./docs/getting-started/first-agent.md) - **A multi-user MCP memory server** with namespaces, roles and tokens. [Multi-user mode](./docs/getting-started/quickstart.md#start-in-multi-user-mode) · [Namespaces and sharing](./docs/features/namespaces-and-sharing.md) - **A code index of your repositories** that coding agents query for definitions, callers and change impact. [Code index](./docs/use-cases/code-intelligence.md) · [Language support and limits](./docs/features/code-index/overview.md#language-support) - **Memories linked to the code they are about**, which follow it through refactors, are flagged when it changes and appear when an agent reads or edits it. [Memory linked to code](./docs/use-cases/memory-linked-to-code.md) - **Lower model cost for coding agents**, as [measured](#measured-results) below. [Coding-agent cost](./docs/use-cases/coding-agent-cost.md) - **Document search with citations (RAG)**, including PDF, `.docx` and `.pptx` files the extractor service converts. [Document search](./docs/use-cases/document-search.md) - **Shared context for multi-agent workflows**: shared memory, task inboxes and decisions. [Multi-agent](./docs/use-cases/multi-agent.md) - **Memory, recall, audit and erasure for autonomous agents.** [Autonomous agents](./docs/use-cases/autonomous-agents.md) - **A record of agent work**, with searchable conversations (when recording is on), session briefs to resume from, runs with their goals, outcomes and model costs when supplied, and PR and tracker history. [Runs and PR history](./docs/use-cases/runs-and-pr-history.md) **Memory for a software factory.** Loom gives implementation and review agents shared lessons, issue context and source provenance across sessions. Scope each principal's access with tokens, await required writes and task handoffs in your application, and recheck code-linked lessons against the current source before review. The same service supports multi-agent workflows and autonomous bots; your orchestration runs the agents, tests and approvals. Offering a tool does not guarantee the model uses it. [Multi-agent workflow](./docs/use-cases/multi-agent.md) · [Autonomous-agent memory](./docs/use-cases/autonomous-agents.md) Every use case, and when another tool fits better: [use cases](./docs/use-cases/index.md). Read [Choosing memory for a software factory](https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom/discussions/939) for memory architecture choices, data ownership and operating responsibilities. Loom is not an in-process library for one agent's short-lived memory, nor an agent framework. [When Loom does not fit](./docs/getting-started/overview.md#when-it-does-not-fit) ## Measured results | Evaluation | With Loom | Without Loom | Efficiency gain | Scope | | ------------------------------ | --------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | | Coding-agent answer quality | **0.84** | 0.78 | **20% lower** model cost | 24 questions × 3 paired runs | | Coding-agent file localization | **96.4%** | 91.4% | **21% lower** model cost | 36 questions × 10 paired runs | | Memory vs full-history answers | **94%** | 90% | **91% fewer** reader prompt tokens | 100 paired LongMemEval-S questions | Both coding setups use Claude Code (`claude-sonnet-5`) on the ClickHouse codebase; cost is the whole session's model bill, excluding Loom's server-side model calls, hosting and indexing. Answer quality measures coverage of a verified answer's key points, with a contradiction penalty. File localization counts whether the right file is among the up to three files the agent is asked to name at the end of its answer. The memory row compares retrieved memories with full conversation history using the same `gpt-5` reader. Token savings exclude memory construction; the 94% vs 90% accuracy difference is descriptive, not statistically established. **Separately, Loom's `memory.ask` configuration scored 96.6% answer accuracy on all 500 LongMemEval-S questions.** This is a product evaluation with its own configured answer models, not the fixed-reader comparison above. Results are specific to the tested workloads. [Protocols and reproducible artifacts](./docs/benchmarks/results.md) · [detailed results](#benchmark-details) · [evaluate on your workload](./docs/getting-started/evaluate.md) ## Get started ### 1. Choose your Docker setup - **Personal use—the default:** no login, localhost-only access and a `dev/local` namespace. One person can connect multiple agents. - **Team use:** authenticated accounts and namespace access controls. [Start in multi-user mode from the first boot](./docs/getting-started/quickstart.md#start-in-multi-user-mode). Both modes support the same Loom features, including configured LLMs and embeddings. Single-user is not a reduced-feature edition. You can also [switch an existing installation without deleting its data](./docs/getting-started/quickstart.md#2-open-the-dashboard); grant new accounts access to the existing namespaces. To try it with nothing installed, open it in a codespace: [![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/ClickHouse/loom?quickstart=1) ([what it runs and who can reach it](./docs/getting-started/quickstart.md#try-it-in-github-codespaces)) For the default personal installation, with Docker installed (on Windows, in a WSL 2 terminal where `docker` works: Docker Desktop with its WSL integration on, or Docker Engine installed in the distribution): ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o loom-install.sh && sh loom-install.sh && rm loom-install.sh ``` Run it from your home directory, or another [directory only you can write to](./docs/getting-started/quickstart.md#fast-path-released-image-no-clone). The installer starts Loom and ClickHouse, applies migrations and prints the dashboard URL: **http://localhost:7777/**; on a new install it then checks that a memory saves and reads back. On a terminal it also offers to connect the coding agents it finds (Claude Code, Codex, VS Code) and, on a new install, opens the dashboard. The image includes the server, workers, dashboard and Python, TypeScript and Go compiler indexers, plus the C++ one on `amd64`; TypeScript dependencies are prepared automatically. [Quickstart and pinned releases](./docs/getting-started/quickstart.md) The installation lives in `~/.loom` (`LOOM_INSTALL_DIR` chooses another directory): the Compose file and the startup settings in `~/.loom/.env`. Running the install command again upgrades in place and keeps your `.env` settings. Keep single-user mode localhost-only. For shared access, follow the [team deployment guide](./docs/operations/deployment.md#identity-modes), including TLS. ### 2. Configure models and API keys **The stock installation boots without keys or network.** Storage, the dashboard, structural code indexing and semantic search work, on a small local embedding model the image carries; the fake LLM gives no AI-generated answers. | Component | Configure for real use | Without configuration | | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Embeddings | Provider, embedding model, dimensions and API key. | `local` (bge-small on CPU): semantic retrieval, weaker than a hosted model. | | LLM | Provider, model and API key. | `fake-echo-1`: no meaningful extraction, summaries or answers. | Open **Settings → Models & keys**, choose both providers and models, enter their keys, then click **Test & apply**. No Docker restart is needed; changing the embedding space rebuilds the existing index. The dashboard's embedding choices are hosted providers: to keep `local` and add an LLM, set the LLM lines in `~/.loom/.env` instead ([Models and keys](docs/getting-started/models-and-keys.md#claude-for-the-llm)). **One OpenAI API key can serve both roles.** Claude needs a separate embedding provider. OpenAI, Gemini and OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoints are supported. Your agent's CLI login or subscription does not supply Loom's provider keys. Prefer environment configuration? Edit `~/.loom/.env`, then recreate the server: ```bash docker compose --project-directory "$HOME/.loom" up -d --force-recreate loom ``` A key alone does not change the pinned models (the local embedder and the fake LLM); set the provider and model too. Saved dashboard settings take precedence over `.env`. Follow [models and API keys](./docs/getting-started/models-and-keys.md) for provider recipes and health checks. **Everything else is in one file.** [`loom.example.yaml`](./loom.example.yaml) lists every setting with its default and what it does, by area: the ClickHouse connection, timeouts and budgets, rate limits, workers, and the `*_enabled` switches that turn features on and off. Set any of them as `LOOM_` in `~/.loom/.env` and recreate the server; a deployment that mounts a config file can set them in a copy of this file instead ([how settings are read](./docs/operations/deployment.md#how-settings-are-read)). One marked `live` also changes while Loom runs: `loom settings set `, or Admin → Deployment settings. `loom settings list --changed` shows what differs from the defaults and where each value came from ([runtime settings](./docs/operations/runtime-settings.md)). ### 3. Connect your agents If the installer connected your agent, skip the commands below. On the machine running a personal installation, the plugins need no token: ```bash # Claude Code claude plugin marketplace add ClickHouse/loom claude plugin install loom@loom # Codex codex plugin marketplace add ClickHouse/loom codex plugin add loom@loom ``` Start a new session; the first one connects to `http://localhost:7777`. In Codex, run `codex` interactively once and approve the plugin's hooks; until then only the tools work. Tell the agent something worth keeping, then ask about it in the next session. For Cursor, on a Teams or Enterprise plan, a team admin can import this repository as a team marketplace; its [Cursor plugin](./docs/features/integrations/cursor.md#plugin), untested in Cursor, installs the MCP entry and Loom's skills. On the machine running a personal installation, the button below adds the [local MCP entry](./docs/features/integrations/cursor.md#mcp-tools), which needs no token: [![Add Loom to Cursor](https://cursor.com/deeplink/mcp-install-dark.svg)](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=loom&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwOi8vbG9jYWxob3N0Ojc3NzcvbWNwP3Rvb2xzZXQ9Y29kaW5nIn0%3D) For VS Code agent mode on the machine running a personal installation, the buttons below add the [local MCP entry](./docs/features/integrations/vscode.md#local-single-user-server), which needs no token: [![Add Loom to VS Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/VS_Code-Add_Loom-0098FF?logo=visualstudiocode&logoColor=white)](https://vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode%3Amcp%2Finstall%3F%257B%2522name%2522%253A%2522loom%2522%252C%2522type%2522%253A%2522http%2522%252C%2522url%2522%253A%2522http%253A%252F%252Flocalhost%253A7777%252Fmcp%2522%257D) [![Add Loom to VS Code Insiders](https://img.shields.io/badge/VS_Code_Insiders-Add_Loom-24bfa5?logo=visualstudiocode&logoColor=white)](https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect?url=vscode-insiders%3Amcp%2Finstall%3F%257B%2522name%2522%253A%2522loom%2522%252C%2522type%2522%253A%2522http%2522%252C%2522url%2522%253A%2522http%253A%252F%252Flocalhost%253A7777%252Fmcp%2522%257D) For a team server, pass `--config server_url=… --config token=…` to Claude Code, or point Codex at it as described in [connect a coding agent](./docs/getting-started/connect-a-coding-agent.md). Create tokens in **Settings → Tokens**. Cursor and other MCP clients, and [the SDK](./docs/getting-started/first-agent.md), are covered there too. ## Why Loom - **Memory that carries forward.** Share decisions and findings across agents and sessions. Each fact records who wrote it, version history and conflict review make corrections traceable, and a namespace can be rolled back to any point in time. [Memory](./docs/concepts/memory.md) - **Code intelligence with evidence.** Find definitions, callers, change impact and relevant tests; connect code to commits, pull requests and issues. Use source locations, completeness signals and per-tier freshness to check a result. [Code index](./docs/features/code-index/overview.md) - **Grounded retrieval.** Search permitted memories, documents, conversations and tracker records. Answers cite their sources; low-confidence retrieval can abstain. [Retrieval](./docs/concepts/retrieval-and-ranking.md) - **Multi-agent handoffs.** Assign work through durable task inboxes with leases, retries, review rules and outcomes. Your agents execute the workflow; Loom preserves the handoffs. [Task queues](./docs/features/tasks-and-decisions.md) - **Control over agent data.** Manage namespace access, provenance, retention, audit records and verified erasure. Context remains queryable in ClickHouse. [Security](./docs/architecture/security.md) ## Integrations | Integration | What it connects | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Claude Code](./docs/features/integrations/claude-code.md), [Codex](./docs/features/integrations/codex.md), [Cursor](./docs/features/integrations/cursor.md) and [other MCP clients](./docs/features/integrations/mcp-clients.md) ([all integrations](./docs/features/integrations/index.md)) | Memory and code intelligence in your existing agent workflow. | | [Python](./docs/reference/python-sdk.md), [TypeScript](./docs/reference/typescript-sdk.md), [Rust](./sdk/rust/README.md), [Go](./sdk/go/README.md), [.NET](./sdk/dotnet/README.md) and [HTTP](./docs/reference/operations.md) | Your own agents and applications. | | [Langfuse](./docs/features/integrations/langfuse.md) | Request traces, model costs, retrieval scores and prompt-version attribution. | | [ClickStack / HyperDX](./docs/features/integrations/clickstack.md) | OpenTelemetry traces, logs and metrics in ClickHouse. | Langfuse and ClickStack are optional integrations, not bundled services in the Docker stack. ## Benchmark details ### Detailed retrieval, reader and code-search results | Evaluation | Result | | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | LongMemEval-S evidence retrieval (500 questions) | **98.6%** of questions with at least one supporting session in the first 30 memories. | | LongMemEval-S fixed `gpt-5` reader (500 questions) | **92.0%** answer accuracy from the top 200 memories. | | LoCoMo (all 10 conversations) | **89.6%** answer accuracy; **90.8%** correct abstentions on adversarial questions. | | MemoryAgentBench fact-question sample (500 questions) | **99.0%** SubEM; **95.7%** token-overlap F1 on generated answers. | | Conceptual code search (36 questions) | Gold-file recall **91.2%** at 5 / **97.2%** at 10; MRR **0.91**. | | SWE-bench Verified file localization (200 issues) | Issues with a changed file in the first 10: **82%** vs **57%** for BM25; **76.5%** in the first 5. | | Tracker duplicate detection (104 pairs) | Recorded older duplicate ranked first **87.5%** of the time. | These measure different tasks, not one aggregate score. SWE-bench measures file localization, not issue resolution. The [results ledger](./docs/benchmarks/results.md) includes scoring definitions, small-sample evaluations, weaker and negative findings, and the full protocols, models and artifacts. [Methodology](./docs/benchmarks/methodology.md) · [coverage and known gaps](./docs/benchmarks/coverage.md) · [run the benchmarks](./docs/benchmarks/running.md) ## Documentation and contributing For shared agent context, code intelligence and permissioned retrieval, start with the [documentation](https://clickhouse.github.io/loom/). For deployment requirements, see the [prerequisites](./docs/getting-started/overview.md#prerequisites). [Deployment](./docs/operations/deployment.md) · [FAQ](./docs/faq.md) · [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Security reporting](./SECURITY.md) · [`llms.txt`](https://clickhouse.github.io/loom/llms.txt) · [`llms-full.txt`](https://clickhouse.github.io/loom/llms-full.txt) Apache-2.0 · [License](./LICENSE) · [Notice](./NOTICE)

[project]
name = "clickhouse-loom-server"
version = "1.3.0"
description = "Loom server (control plane). Shared-production agent memory + knowledge plane on ClickHouse. Distributed as a Docker image (ghcr.io/clickhouse/loom) — `pip install` is for local dev / Docker-image build only; do NOT run the server from pip in production."
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
readme = "README.md"
authors = [{ name = "ClickHouse, Inc." }]
urls = { Homepage = "https://clickhouse.github.io/loom/", Repository = "https://github.com/ClickHouse/loom" }
# PEP 541: PyPI rejects uploads whose primary classifier is "Private ::
# Do Not Upload". Loom's server is a shared-production data plane,
# deployed multi-user / multi-agent against ClickHouse Cloud or self-
# hosted OSS ClickHouse — not something developers pip-install on a
# laptop. The Docker image at ghcr.io/clickhouse/loom is the canonical
# server artefact. The SDK (`clickhouse-loom` at sdk/python/) is what's
# published to PyPI for application developers.
classifiers = ["Private :: Do Not Upload"]

dependencies = [
  "fastapi>=0.118",
  "uvicorn[standard]>=0.50", # ssl_context_factory, and a worker exiting 3 stops all (server/core/tls.py)
  "pydantic>=2.9",
  "pydantic-settings>=2.5",
  # The YAML settings file (server/settings/_file.py); uvicorn[standard] pulls it in too.
  "pyyaml>=6.0",
  "clickhouse-connect>=1.7", # older ones drop milliseconds (<1.2) or bind a naive datetime as local time
  "aiohttp>=3.10",           # clickhouse-connect's async client requires it
  "anyio>=4",                # a wait no cancellation cuts short: server.core.shielded
  "httpx[http2]>=0.27",
  "idna>=3.7",               # UTS 46 host names: server.settings.catalog.ascii_host
  "dnspython>=2.6",          # a cancellable lookup for names a tenant chooses: server.core.hosts
  "tenacity>=9.0",
  "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.10",
  # OpenTelemetry: ship spans + logs to HyperDX / ClickStack's OTLP
  # collector. ClickStack is the OTel consumer in the Loom stack
  # (docs/features/integrations/clickstack.md); this wires the producer side.
  "opentelemetry-api>=1.45.2",
  "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.45.2",
  "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.27",
  "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.48b0",
  "opentelemetry-instrumentation-httpx>=0.48b0",
  # Logs API + the SDK's logging.Handler bridge that auto-attaches
  # trace_id/span_id from the active span. Logs land alongside traces
  # in HyperDX, correlated by trace_id so a single click jumps from
  # one to the other.
  "opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging>=0.48b0",
  # Password hashing for email+password sign-in. argon2id is the
  # modern OWASP-preferred KDF; argon2-cffi is the canonical Python
  # binding. Used by server.auth.passwords (hash / verify / rehash).
  "argon2-cffi>=23.1",

  # English Porter (Snowball) stemmer for verb canonicalization in
  # entity_triples. Pure-Python, no model download. Used by
  # `canonicalize_verb` in server.memory.app.retrieval; the
  # stemmer collapses inflected forms (visited/visiting/visits → visit)
  # so triple-store matches across write/query verb tense.
  "snowballstemmer>=2.2",
  # RE2 (linear-time, no backtracking) for caller-supplied regexes matched in
  # Python: code.grep's line step and context.fetch. Same engine as ClickHouse's
  # match(), so a pattern means the same thing in both places.
  "google-re2>=1.1",
  # Postgres for the Postgres storage profile (LOOM_STORAGE_AUTHORITY=postgres): the async
  # driver and its pool. Imported only when that profile is configured.
  "asyncpg>=0.30",
  # lemmagen3 (the English lemmatizer) is the `[lemma]` extra below, not a
  # core dep: it ships no wheel and compiles against Python.h, and a host
  # that only wants the `loom` CLI (`loom up`) may have no build toolchain.
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Lemmagen3 English lemmatizer — covers irregular morphology Snowball misses
# (went/go, mice/mouse, children/child). Matches ClickHouse's
# lemmatize('en', ...) byte-for-byte: deploy/lemmagen3/en.bin, which ClickHouse
# loads, is the model this wheel ships. The Docker image installs it (Dockerfile EXTRAS) and so
# does `[dev]`; `server/memory/domain/lemmatize.py` imports it lazily and falls
# open to the plain tokens when it is absent, so a host running only the CLI
# never compiles it. A host-run *server* without it writes
# unlemmatized `content_excerpt_lemma` — install `.[lemma]` for `make server`.
lemma = [
  "lemmagen3>=3.3",
]
dev = [
  "lemmagen3>=3.3",                    # the server's own lexical leg; tests exercise it
  "clickhouse-loom-server[aws]",       # the export-analytics tests exercise boto3
  "clickhouse-loom-server[extractor]", # the extractor's parser tests parse every format
  "pytest>=8.0",
  "pytest-asyncio>=0.24",
  "pytest-httpx>=0.32",
  "pytest-rerunfailures>=15.0",
  "pytest-cov>=5.0",
  # Unit tests run in a random order with the seed CI prints (tests/README.md).
  "pytest-randomly>=3.15",
  # The unit job spreads the suite over the runner's cores (`-n auto`).
  "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
  # The ratchets count mypy errors and ruff findings per file; a new release
  # moves those counts with no code change, so both are pinned.
  "mypy==2.3.1",
  "types-PyYAML>=6.0",
  "ruff==0.16.9",
  "build>=1.0",
  # Translation table verification uses the documentation site's parser.
  "Markdown==3.11.2",
  "mdx-truly-sane-lists==1.3",
  "pymdown-extensions==12.3",
  "markdown-it-py==4.0.0",
]
# Operator CLI extra — needed only by `dev/loom_ingest.py` to fetch an S3
# source. Not a server dep; the CLI lazy-imports it with an actionable error
# message when missing. It parses nothing: the server's extractor does.
ingest = [
  "boto3>=1.36", # the document bucket client's checksum options; see `aws`
]
# The reference extractor's parsers (extractor/loom_extractor/), for its tests in this
# environment. The server never imports them; the service installs extractor/pyproject.toml.
extractor = [
  "cryptography>=50,<51", # pypdf's AES: a PDF encrypted with an owner password alone opens
  "pyarrow>=26,<27",      # Parquet: a major may change what its decoder accepts, reviewed before a bump
  "pypdf>=6.21,<7",
  "sqlglot>=30.27,<31",   # imports sqlglot.tokenizer_core, which a major may move
]
# `loom export-analytics` uploads to S3 under an assumed role, and
# LOOM_DOCUMENT_OBJECT_STORE=s3 keeps document originals in a bucket; native Bedrock
# model calls use its credential chain and signing. Ships in the image.
aws = [
  # 1.36: the first whose client config takes the checksum options the document
  # bucket client sets (put_object's IfNoneMatch came in 1.35.2)
  "boto3>=1.36",
]
# Code intelligence plane: tree-sitter parses C++ for
# the fast tier, numpy runs the weekly PageRank. Needed only when the code
# workers / `loom code` CLI are used — all imports are lazy, the server
# boots without these while the workers stay disabled.
code = [
  "tree-sitter>=0.23",
  "tree-sitter-cpp>=0.23",
  "tree-sitter-python>=0.23",
  "tree-sitter-bash>=0.23",
  # TypeScript (+ tsx), JavaScript and Rust
  "tree-sitter-typescript>=0.23",
  "tree-sitter-javascript>=0.23",
  "tree-sitter-rust>=0.23",
  # Go and Java (lane parsers + SQL islands)
  "tree-sitter-go>=0.23",
  "tree-sitter-java>=0.23",
  "numpy>=1.26",
]
# scripts/scip_harness only (protobuf parse of scip-clang output). Never a
# server dep — the server ingests the normalized JSON delta.
scip = [
  "protobuf>=7.35.1",
]
# Local CPU embedder extras, for LOOM_EMBEDDING_MODEL=local*: the image installs
# them and the released stack embeds with them. fastembed pulls in onnxruntime
# (~80MB wheel); the model files are pinned in server/embedding/local_models.py.
# Lazy-imported by server/embedding/local.py with an actionable error
# message when missing.
local-embedder = [
  "fastembed>=0.9.1", # the first to allow pillow 13, which fixes critical CVEs in 12.x
]

[project.scripts]
# `loom` CLI — bundled INSIDE the Docker image for operator use.
# Not exposed via PyPI (root pyproject is Private :: Do Not Upload).
# Operators run it via `docker exec loom-server loom mint-token ...` or
# the equivalent on whatever orchestrator hosts the container. From a clone,
# `pip install -e .` puts it on the host too — no compiler needed:
# lemmagen3 is in the `[lemma]` extra.
#   loom up            # boot the local stack + print how to connect
#   loom serve         # boot the control plane (the image runs uvicorn directly)
#   loom migrate       # apply schema migrations
#   loom mint-token    # issue a JWT (operator's path; needs LOOM_JWT_SECRET)
loom = "server.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
# Server-only wheel. The SDK has its own pyproject at sdk/python/
# (published to PyPI as `clickhouse-loom`); this root pyproject builds
# the server wheel that the Dockerfile installs into the image.
packages = ["server"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# pytest-asyncio 0.23+ defaults to a fresh event loop per fixture and
# per test, which breaks the integration tests' module-scope async
# fixtures (they connect a CH client at module scope and reuse it
# across tests). The fixture's awaitables bind to loop A, then test 2
# runs on loop B and tries to await them — "Future attached to a
# different loop". Setting both scopes to "session" gives every test
# and fixture in the process one shared loop. The integration tests talk to the control plane over HTTP
# (separate process), so in-process loop sharing has no contention
# risk.
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"
asyncio_default_test_loop_scope = "session"
testpaths = ["tests"]
# The reference extractor is its own package, outside the server wheel.
pythonpath = ["extractor"]
# A mark that is not registered here or by a plugin is an error, not a
# silent no-op: a typo in a tier marker would otherwise leave the test in the
# default tier. tests/README.md says which CI job runs each tier.
strict_markers = true
markers = [
  "slow: takes more than a few seconds; runs in the integration job, never in unit",
  "destructive: stops merges, drops or rewrites shared objects; needs a disposable ClickHouse",
  "provider: calls a real LLM or embedding provider; skips without its key",
  "recovery: kills, restarts or resumes a worker, saga or migration mid-flight",
  "copy_head_check: a unit test that runs the post-copy head re-check (off by default in unit)",
  "doctor_tier_read: a unit test that runs loom doctor's read of the failing code-index tiers (off by default in unit)",
  "claim_cap: a unit test that runs the namespace gate's claim cap (off by default in unit)",
]

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["server", "sdk/python/loom", "extractor/loom_extractor"]
mypy_path = "extractor"
exclude = ["tests/"]

# Optional packages imported lazily with a fallback, present in some
# environments and not others: lemmagen3 comes with `[dev]` and `[lemma]`,
# fastembed with `[local-embedder]`, and tiktoken is undeclared (the
# embedders approximate token counts without it). mypy's error for them
# would differ by environment; their call sites are typed through local
# Protocols.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["fastembed", "fastembed.*", "lemmagen3", "tiktoken", "tiktoken.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# pyarrow ships no type information; the extractor's Parquet reader types what it reads as Any.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["pyarrow", "pyarrow.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# google-re2 ships no type information; server/core/caller_regex.py types its result as Any.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["re2"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# asyncpg (the Postgres memory authority's driver) ships no type information.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["asyncpg", "asyncpg.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# boto3 is the SDK's and the server's optional `aws` extra (a bot key in Secrets
# Manager, `loom export-analytics`, the document bucket), and ships no types.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["boto3", "boto3.*", "botocore", "botocore.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# The SDK's framework adapters: no framework is installed here. Each framework is an SDK
# extra, which `make test-sdk-adapters` installs to type-check its adapter; LangGraph and
# Strands are typed through structural twins. Without the framework the base is Any,
# which strict mode refuses to subclass.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
  "langchain_core",
  "langchain_core.*",
  "llama_index",
  "llama_index.*",
  "agents",
  "agents.*",
  "crewai",
  "crewai.*",
  "autogen_core",
  "autogen_core.*",
  "pydantic_ai",
  "pydantic_ai.*",
  "ag2",
  "ag2.*",
  "agno",
  "agno.*",
  "haystack",
  "haystack.*",
  "agent_framework",
  "agent_framework.*",
  "anthropic",
  "anthropic.*",
  "google.adk",
  "google.adk.*",
  "google.genai",
  "google.genai.*",
  "langgraph",
  "langgraph.*",
  "strands",
  "strands.*",
  "pipecat",
  "pipecat.*",
  "dspy",
  "dspy.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["loom.integrations.*"]
disallow_subclassing_any = false

[tool.coverage.run]
# Coverage is measured over the unit suite in CI: each `unit` part writes its data,
# the `unit-coverage` job combines them and applies the floors. Integration
# tests run the server out-of-process so they don't contribute to in-process
# coverage; treat this as a unit-coverage floor, not a total.
source = ["server", "sdk/python/loom"]
# The C tracer, which `sys.settrace(None)` pauses: the extraction tests' time bounds
# (tests/unit/test_document_extraction.py `_cpu`) time the code with it off, through
# `untraced` (tests/unit/code_fixtures.py).
core = "ctrace"
omit = ["*/tests/*", "*/__pycache__/*"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
# Keep precision modest — this is a regression guard, not a vanity metric.
precision = 0

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
# First-party packages: the server from the root, the reference extractor from its directory.
src = [".", "extractor"]
target-version = "py312"
# The SDK supports Python 3.11 (sdk/python/pyproject.toml requires-python), so
# its lint rules must not rewrite it to newer syntax. The wheel smoke test runs
# on that floor too.
per-file-target-version = { "sdk/python/**" = "py311", "scripts/gates/sdk_wheel_smoke.py" = "py311" }
# Generated protobuf bindings keep their generated form.
extend-exclude = ["scripts/scip_harness/vendor"]

[tool.ruff.format]
# Formatting is `ruff format`; these paths keep their bytes.
exclude = [
  # Inputs whose exact bytes and line numbers tests assert on.
  "tests/fixtures/**",
  "scripts/scip_harness/vendor/**",
  # Generated by scripts/codegen/sdk_py_gen.py and sdk_py_client_gen.py; their --check compares bytes.
  "sdk/python/loom/ops.py",
  "sdk/python/loom/client.py",
  # Extractor modules: their code tokens are the code index's version stamp
  # and a formatter may rewrite string quotes, which would re-index every
  # repository. Kept in step with extractor_stamp.EXTRACTOR_MODULES by
  # tests/unit/test_format_excludes_extractor_modules.py.
  "server/code/domain/extract/call_guards.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/callee_outline.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/chunker.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/context_text.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/cpp_receivers.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/crossref.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/edges_treesitter.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/lang_bash.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/lang_python.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/py_layouts.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/py_library_methods.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/py_members.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/py_receivers.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/registration.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/spans.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/tokenize.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/treesitter.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/ts_config.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/ts_receivers.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/ts_reexports.py",
  "server/code/domain/extract/ts_workspace.py",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "B", "UP", "ASYNC", "BLE", "RUF100"]
# PLR0915 runs from scripts/gates/function_length_gate.py, not from this config:
# its noqa comments are used there.
external = ["PLR0915"]

# Tests get more slack on line length — assertions, SQL string literals,
# and JSON fixtures often run long and reflowing them harms readability.
# Production code keeps the 100-char rule.
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["E501"]
# Generated by scripts/codegen/sdk_py_gen.py and sdk_py_client_gen.py: their file-level noqa is the generator's, not ours to prune.
"sdk/python/loom/ops.py" = ["RUF100"]
"sdk/python/loom/client.py" = ["RUF100"]
# Bench scripts are short-lived runners (one-shot, asyncio.run from
# main). ASYNC230/240 catch blocking IO inside async funcs — meant
# for library code where it stalls the event loop. Bench scripts
# don't have loop contention to worry about.
"bench/**/*.py" = ["ASYNC230", "ASYNC240"]
# These two modules carry the LLM extraction / query-enrichment prompts:
# multi-line few-shot JSON examples plus inline graph SQL. The long lines ARE the string content;
# reflowing them either changes what the model sees or splits SQL awkwardly,
# and `# noqa` can't target a line inside a triple-quoted literal. Same
# rationale as the tests exemption above.
"server/memory/app/extract/*.py" = ["E501"]
# Holds the extraction LLM prompt literals (few-shot JSON examples). Same
# rationale: the long lines ARE the string content.
"server/memory/domain/extraction_prompts.py" = ["E501"]
"server/memory/app/retrieval/*.py" = ["E501"]
# Holds the search-pipeline LLM prompt literals.
"server/memory/domain/search_prompts.py" = ["E501"]

decision_reasons: High-severity capability requires manual security review

quality_controls.evidence: Canonical GitHub identity and retrieval timestamp
quality_controls.name: provenance

repository.description: Brigade Stack: run coding agents anywhere and keep one record of the work. Shared tasks, claims, verification receipts, handoffs, and MCP and skills sync for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and T3 Code.
repository.name: brigade
repository.readme:
Run agents anywhere. Same memory everywhere.

Website · Docs · Quickstart · Compare · Changelog

BrigadeStack gives the agent tools you already use one shared memory and one set of MCP servers and skills. It keeps a record of the work they check. Install with pipx (Python 3.11 or newer) or npm (Node.js `^22.15.0 || >=23.11.0`). The command is `brigadestack`. `brigadestack` on PyPI is the Python package. The `brigade-cli` compatibility package and the `@escoffier-labs/brigade` npm package install the same CLI as `brigade`, so existing users keep their command and `pipx upgrade brigade-cli` keeps working. ```bash pipx install brigadestack npm install -g brigadestack ``` Sections marked * describe the 0.32.0 beta. It is published as daily pre-release builds of `brigadestack`, which install the `brigade` command: `pipx install --pip-args='--pre' brigadestack`. Stable is 0.31.0. ## Shared memory, shared tools Claude Code, Codex and Cursor each keep their own notes and MCP config, so what one agent learns on Monday is gone when another starts on Tuesday. BrigadeStack keeps memory as markdown cards in your repository. An agent that learns something durable writes a handoff. A reviewer files it as a card. Commit the card, and any checkout finds it with `brigadestack memory search`. Claude Code also gets recall at session start. Codex gets memory through its handoff inbox and an agent-run `memory search`.

The commands behind that picture This is real output, with the home directory shortened to `~`. ```console $ cd ~/api $ brigadestack handoff draft --type decision \ --title "Payments client retry policy" \ --summary "Retries stop after 3 attempts with jittered backoff." \ --fact "Backoff starts at 200 ms and doubles." \ --fact "A 4xx response is never retried." \ --action create-card --target-card payments-retry-policy.md \ --content-file card.md handoff draft: ~/api/.codex/memory-handoffs/20261118-014553-payments-client-retry-policy.md id: 20261118-014553-payments-client-retry-policy inbox: .codex/memory-handoffs action: create-card target_card: payments-retry-policy.md lint: ok $ cp card.md memory/cards/payments-retry-policy.md $ git add memory && git commit -qm "memory: payments retry policy" $ git worktree add -q ../api-2 -b second && cd ../api-2 $ brigadestack memory search "retry backoff" memory search: retry backoff (1 match(es)) - memory/cards/payments-retry-policy.md [0.74] payments-retry-policy ```
### One list of MCP servers and skills MCP servers and skills follow the same rule as memory. List a server once in `.brigade/mcp.json`, and `brigadestack mcp sync` writes it into each set-up tool's config, through adapters for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Grok. Antigravity needs `--user-scope`, and VS Code is included when the repository has a `.vscode` folder. It previews until `--write` and keeps Codex and OpenCode native auth*. `brigadestack skills sync --target all` previews the same way for skills. * In the 0.32.0 beta, sync also keeps Claude Code's own auth helper and refuses to remove or re-point an entry that has one.

## Then prove it "Tests pass" is a claim. `brigadestack work verify run` turns it into a record. It runs the command and keeps the command, the exit code, the logs and a fingerprint of the tree that was tested. Another agent can open it and see what ran against which code. Records live under `.brigade/work/verify-runs/`, one folder per run. A failing command leaves a failed record too.

### Know what a change touches The code graph is a local index of your repository's symbols and the calls between them. `brigadestack setup` installs the optional engine, and `brigadestack code sync` builds the index. `brigadestack code callers ` shows who calls a function, `impact` adds callees, and `affected ` lists the tests that reach changed files. Below is a real answer for one function here.

## Modes* `strict` is the default. Checks run through `brigadestack work verify run`, and Claude Code's stop hook asks for a record before a session finishes. `observe` records checks and blocks nothing. `off` drops the check rules and keeps memory and briefs. Safety rails (secret scanning and pre-push checks) are a separate setting, on by default in every mode. * `observe` and the names `strict` and `off` are in the 0.32.0 beta, as the capture shows. Version 0.31.0 calls them `engineer` and `yolo` and has no `observe`. The beta still accepts the old names. ```console $ brigade work mode show work mode: strict; safety rails: on (~/api) $ brigade work mode set observe work mode: observe; safety rails: on (~/api) $ brigade work mode set off work mode: off; safety rails: on (~/api) ``` ## Quick start Wire a repository, write a first handoff, and run a first check. Add `--dry-run` to the first command to preview it. ```bash brigadestack operator quickstart --target . --harnesses codex,claude brigadestack handoff draft --type setup --title "Test command" \ --summary "Run pytest -q from the repo root before every push." \ --action no-card --target-document TOOLS.md \ --content "Run pytest -q from the repo root." brigadestack work verify run --command "git diff --check" ``` The first command writes `.brigade/`, a handoff inbox for each tool you name, and the MCP config. The second drafts a handoff, and lint refuses what the ingester would reject. The third records the command, exit code and logs. Keep `.brigade/` state out of commits unless you mean to share it. See the [first 10 minutes](https://github.com/escoffier-labs/brigade/blob/main/docs/first-10-minutes.md). ## Works with | Tool | What you get | | --- | --- | | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode | Workspace instructions, handoff inboxes, and MCP and skill config. | | ChatGPT Dot | Memory, skills, Hub messages and T3 fleet dispatch, through a connector you host. | | Claude Duet | Memory, skills, Hub messages and read-only fleet views, through a connector you host. | | T3 Code | Session presence only. | Setup guides: [Dot](https://github.com/escoffier-labs/brigade/blob/main/docs/grokbot-dot.md) and [Duet](https://github.com/escoffier-labs/brigade/blob/main/docs/duet-connector.md). ## Across machines Agents on several machines share memory through a hub service you run on a network you control. A card pushed from a laptop turns up in a search on a desktop. Task ownership, messages and model policy live in the same place. The [fleet docs](https://github.com/escoffier-labs/brigade/blob/main/docs/fleet-sync.md) cover setup. ## Limits A check record shows what ran. It does not show that the tests are good. A handoff is a draft until someone files it as a card. The packaged hub and the Dot listener are Linux only. Dot and Duet are not woken instantly: each checks for work when a session or scheduled run starts. ## MCP servers - `brigadestack memory serve-mcp --stdio` serves memory cards, the work brief and `write_handoff`, which drafts a handoff and never edits a card. - `brigadestack skills serve-mcp --stdio` serves the reviewed skill registry, read-only: search, read and lint skills.

About the downloads badge The downloads badge sums `brigadestack` and `brigade-cli` on PyPI (excluding mirrors) and `@escoffier-labs/brigade` on npm over the same 30 completed UTC days. Downloads include automation and do not count unique people. The [metric JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/escoffier-labs/brigade/download-metrics/downloads.json) records each source, the period, and the last successful refresh. npm platform companions are excluded. Daily refreshes retain the previous metric if a source fails validation or its latest day is more than three UTC days old.
