      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          uv sync --extra treesitter-full --extra memgraph
          uv add --dev pyinstaller

      - name: Build binary
        run: uv run python build_binary.py

      - name: Test binary
        run: ./dist/code-graph-rag-* --version

  # Every other job installs from uv.lock, so no job exercises the dependency
  # resolution a real `pip install code-graph-rag` performs: newest versions
  # satisfying the pyproject.toml floors. This job does, so a dependency that
  # ships a breaking major inside our declared range fails here instead of in a
  # user's terminal a week later (#1096).
  wheel-fresh-resolution:
    name: Wheel Smoke (unlocked resolution)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20

    steps:
      # This job installs freshly resolved third-party packages and then runs
      # repository code, so it must not leave the workflow token in the local
      # git config for that code to read.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # cargo (under the crate's wheel build) and pip trust the system store,
      # and the runner's ca-certificates may still carry distrusted eMudhra
      # roots: deselect them before anything is fetched.
      - name: Distrust the eMudhra roots
        run: sudo bash scripts/distrust_ca_roots.sh

      - name: Build wheel
        run: uv build --wheel

      # code-graph-rag requires cgr-graph-rs, which publish.yml uploads
      # first; this commit's own build stands in for it, so the PR is
      # tested against the crate it carries.
      - name: Build the cgr-graph-rs wheel
        run: uv build --wheel rust/cgr_graph_rs --out-dir dist-rust

      # Deliberately plain venv + pip: uv.lock must not participate.
      - name: Install the wheel with unlocked resolution
        run: |
          python -m venv .fresh-venv
          # The venv's bundled pip may predate the emSign distrust (pip
          # 26.2.2), so it fetches only pip itself, the release
          # scripts/pip-requirements.txt pins by SHA-256 and Dependabot keeps
          # current.
          ./.fresh-venv/bin/python -m pip install --require-hashes -r scripts/pip-requirements.txt
          # Both wheels are named, so pip has to take this build of the crate
          # even when PyPI carries a newer one in range; everything else
          # resolves unlocked.
          ./.fresh-venv/bin/python -m pip install dist/*.whl dist-rust/*.whl

      - name: Record resolved dependency versions
        run: ./.fresh-venv/bin/python -m pip list

      - name: Smoke the freshly resolved install
        run: |
          ./.fresh-venv/bin/python -c "import codebase_rag"
          ./.fresh-venv/bin/cgr --version
          ./.fresh-venv/bin/python scripts/smoke_wheel.py

  pr-title-check:
    name: PR Title Convention
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # The action reads the pull request's current title through the API.
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check PR title format
        uses: amannn/action-semantic-pull-request@2252a14e810aa9b85c2d560bd7070c802206ecf6 # v6.1.2
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          types: |
            build
            chore
            ci
            docs
            feat
            fix
            perf
            refactor
            prefactor
            revert
            style
            test
          requireScope: false
          subjectPattern: ^.+$
          subjectPatternError: |
            The subject "{subject}" found in the pull request title "{title}"
            didn't match the configured pattern. Please ensure that the subject
            starts with a lowercase letter.
          wip: false
          validateSingleCommit: false
          validateSingleCommitMatchesPrTitle: false

  go-frontend:
    name: Go Frontend
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ">=1.27.2"
          cache-dependency-path: codebase_rag/parsers/go_frontend/gotypes/go.sum

      - name: Key the uv cache on dependencies, not the project version
        shell: bash
        run: |
          awk 'skip && /^version = / { skip = 0; next }
               { skip = /^name = "code-graph-rag"\r?$/; print }' \
            uv.lock > "$RUNNER_TEMP/uv-deps.lock"

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: ${{ runner.temp }}/uv-deps.lock

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          uv sync --extra treesitter-full --extra test --group dev

      # Build the bundled tool explicitly so a Go compile error is an
      # attributable failure here, not a mysterious skip inside pytest. Deps
      # resolve from the module cache, pinned by go.sum.
      - name: Build the bundled gotypes tool
        working-directory: codebase_rag/parsers/go_frontend/gotypes
        env:
          GOTOOLCHAIN: local
        run: go build ./...

      - name: Run Go frontend tests
        run: |
          uv run --no-sync pytest codebase_rag/tests/test_go_frontend.py -v --tb=short

  # Tests that need a toolchain skip where it is missing, and the unit jobs
  # install only Go: `tsc`, a .NET 10 SDK and Lua were absent on every runner,
  # so a test that needs one never ran, and #3628 failed only off CI. This job
  # installs them and runs every test file that probes for one.
  toolchain-tests:
    name: Toolchain Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: ">=1.27.2"
          cache-dependency-path: codebase_rag/parsers/go_frontend/gotypes/go.sum

      # The C# oracle targets net10.0 (evals/oracles/csharp_oracle/Oracle.csproj).
      - name: Set up .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@26b0ec14cb23fa6904739307f278c14f94c95bf1 # v5.4.0
        with:
          dotnet-version: "10.0.x"

      # `tsc` from the TypeScript oracle's lockfile, the version the evals
      # already pin, rather than an unpinned global install.
      - name: Install the TypeScript compiler and Lua
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix evals/oracles/ts_oracle
          echo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/evals/oracles/ts_oracle/node_modules/.bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends lua5.4

      - name: Show the toolchains
        run: |
          go version
          dotnet --list-sdks
          node --version
          tsc --version
          javac -version
          lua5.4 -v
          cargo --version

      - name: Key the uv cache on dependencies, not the project version
        shell: bash
        run: |
          awk 'skip && /^version = / { skip = 0; next }
               { skip = /^name = "code-graph-rag"\r?$/; print }' \
            uv.lock > "$RUNNER_TEMP/uv-deps.lock"

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: ${{ runner.temp }}/uv-deps.lock

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          uv sync --extra treesitter-full --extra test --group dev

      # Every test file that looks for a toolchain before running. `-rs`
      # prints why anything still skipped, so a toolchain the job lost shows.
      - name: Run the toolchain-dependent tests
        run: |
          mapfile -t files < <(grep -rlE \
            'shutil\.which\("(go|dotnet|dotnet-trace|tsc|node|javac|java|lua|php|phpunit|cargo|dart)"|needs_tsc|needs_javac|oracle_available|go_available|java_available|cargo_available|lua_available|dotnet' \
            codebase_rag/tests --include='test_*.py' | sort)
          echo "${#files[@]} test files"
          uv run --no-sync pytest -n auto -m "not integration" --tb=short -rs "${files[@]}"

  # The graphs of pinned public repositories, one or more per language
  # (fixtures/reference_graphs, issue #3629). A change to what the indexer
  # records must come with the regenerated graph, so it shows in the pull
  # request; the second and third runs index a copy at another path under
  # another hash seed and must give the same graph.
  reference-graphs:
    name: Reference Graphs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          submodules: recursive
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Key the uv cache on dependencies, not the project version
        shell: bash
        run: |
          awk 'skip && /^version = / { skip = 0; next }
               { skip = /^name = "code-graph-rag"\r?$/; print }' \
            uv.lock > "$RUNNER_TEMP/uv-deps.lock"

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: ${{ runner.temp }}/uv-deps.lock

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # What the graphs are recorded with (REFERENCE_EXTRAS in
      # codebase_rag/constants/reference_graphs.py): every tier's extra.
      # Without ast-grep, Ruby and shell files give no nodes; the check
      # compares fixtures/reference_graphs/environment.txt first and names
      # what this machine cannot parse.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --extra treesitter-full --extra ast-grep

      # Keyed on the manifest: a pinned commit never changes, so a hit is
      # always the same checkout.
      - name: Cache the pinned repositories
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/cgr-reference-repos
          key: reference-repos-${{ hashFiles('fixtures/reference_graphs/repos.json') }}

      - name: Check the reference graphs
        run: uv run --no-sync python scripts/reference_graphs.py check --runs 3

  rust-graph-core:
    name: Rust Graph Core
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # rust/cgr_graph_rs (published as cgr-graph-rs, a default dependency on
    # the platforms it has wheels for) runs the embedded graph's whole-graph
    # procedures, its Cypher parser, the ingestor's batch writes and result
    # decoding (issue #386), and the indexer's definition hashes on
    # py-tree-sitter's own trees. Its own tests check the algorithms and the
    # grammar; the Python tests check it returns and writes exactly what
    # the Python implementations it replaces do, and run the engine's
    # suites with it installed. rust-wheels.yml builds and tests the wheels.
    timeout-minutes: 20

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Key the uv cache on dependencies, not the project version
        shell: bash
        run: |
          awk 'skip && /^version = / { skip = 0; next }
               { skip = /^name = "code-graph-rag"\r?$/; print }' \
            uv.lock > "$RUNNER_TEMP/uv-deps.lock"

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: ${{ runner.temp }}/uv-deps.lock

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Test the crate
        run: cargo test --release --manifest-path rust/cgr_graph_rs/Cargo.toml

      # The checkout's crate is a path source, so the sync builds it.
      - name: Install cgr with the extension
        run: uv sync --extra test --group dev

      # The wheel carries every linked crate's licence; a dependency change
      # must regenerate the file before it can ship.
      - name: Check the crates' licences are listed
        run: uv run --no-sync python scripts/generate_rust_licenses.py --check

      - name: Check it against the Python procedures and parser
        run: |
          uv run --no-sync pytest codebase_rag/tests/test_embedded_graph_rust.py codebase_rag/tests/test_embedded_graph_rust_parser.py codebase_rag/tests/test_embedded_graph_native.py codebase_rag/tests/test_native_trees.py --tb=short

      - name: Run the engine's tests on the Rust parser
        run: |
          uv run --no-sync pytest codebase_rag/tests/test_embedded_graph_engine.py codebase_rag/tests/test_embedded_graph_memgraph_parity.py codebase_rag/tests/test_embedded_graph_default.py --tb=short

  greptile-gate:
    name: Greptile 5/5 Gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Every pull request: Greptile reviews forks, Dependabot and every base,
    # and greptile.json has it review each push and draft. The gate fails
    # only on a score below 5/5; with Greptile absent (out of credits,
    # paused) it passes with a warning, so billing never blocks a merge.
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    # The script waits up to 10 min for Greptile to start and up to 45 min
    # for a review in progress to post its score; this cap only bounds a hang.
    timeout-minutes: 55
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # Greptile's score is in its summary comment on the pull request, and
      # its "Greptile Review" check run shows whether a review is in flight.
      pull-requests: read
      checks: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Fail if Greptile scores the head commit below 5/5
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: python3 scripts/greptile_gate.py "$PR" "$HEAD_SHA"

  sonar-gate:
    name: Sonar Zero Issues Gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Mirror the eligibility of the SonarCloud Analysis job in
    # sonarcloud.yml (PRs targeting main, excluding Dependabot and fork
    # heads): a PR that never gets analyzed must skip the gate instead of
    # polling for an analysis that cannot exist.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      && github.event.pull_request.base.ref == 'main'
      && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'
      && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    # The polling loop below does the waiting (it holds out for as long as
    # SonarCloud Analysis is queued or running); this cap only bounds a hang,
    # and covers that job's 70 min cap, a late start and the publish window.
    timeout-minutes: 110
    permissions:
      # checks: read backs the check-runs API call that detects a failed
      # SonarCloud Analysis job, so the gate fails fast instead of waiting
      # out the full deadline for an analysis that will never arrive.
      checks: read
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Require a SonarCloud analysis of the head commit with zero open issues
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PROJECT_KEY: vitali87_code-graph-rag
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # The merge gate: a pull request is mergeable ONLY when SonarCloud
          # has analyzed the CURRENT head commit and reports zero open issues
          # on the pull request. The built-in "Sonar way" quality gate passes
          # with new issues of low severity (its conditions are ratings, not
          # counts), so this job enforces the stricter bar the project wants:
          # every issue fixed, or explicitly resolved (accepted / false
          # positive) in the SonarCloud UI. Both endpoints are public for
          # public projects, so no token is needed. Analysis lands minutes
          # after the SonarCloud Analysis job finishes, so poll until the
          # reported analyzed commit is this exact commit. The window for
          # publishing restarts while the analysis job is queued or running,
          # so a job that starts late or runs long is not cut short (within
          # this job's own cap); the first deadline covers a job that never
          # shows up at all.
          publish_window=900
          deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 3600 ))
          while :; do
            analyzed=$(curl -sf "https://sonarcloud.io/api/project_pull_requests/list?project=$PROJECT_KEY" \
              | jq -r --arg pr "$PR" \
                  '.pullRequests[] | select(.key == $pr) | .commit.sha // empty' \
              || true)
            if [ "$analyzed" = "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
              issues=$(curl -sf "https://sonarcloud.io/api/issues/search?componentKeys=$PROJECT_KEY&pullRequest=$PR&resolved=false&ps=100" \
                || true)
              total=$(printf '%s' "$issues" | jq -r '.total // empty' || true)
              if [ -z "$total" ]; then
                echo "Issue search returned no usable payload, retrying ..."
              elif [ "$total" = "0" ]; then
                echo "✅ SonarCloud analyzed $HEAD_SHA and reports zero open issues"
                exit 0
              else
                echo "❌ SonarCloud reports $total open issue(s) on this pull request:"
                printf '%s' "$issues" | jq -r \
                  '.issues[] | "  - [\(.severity)] \(.component | sub("^[^:]*:"; "")):\(.line // "?") \(.message) (\(.rule))"'
                echo "Fix them and push, or resolve them as accepted/false positive in SonarCloud."
                exit 1
              fi
            else
              # Fail fast when the producer is already dead: a SonarCloud
              # Analysis job that completed without success will never
              # publish an analysis of this commit, so waiting out the
              # deadline would only delay the same failure. A queued or
              # in-progress run holds the verdict open: a rerun sits at
              # started_at null while queued, which jq sorts before every
              # real timestamp, so only the completed runs are ranked and
              # any active run suppresses the fast fail until it finishes.
              # An unreadable check-runs reply (rate limit, outage) is null,
              # which jq cannot iterate, so `active` falls back to 1 and the
              # verdict stays open instead of reading as "no job".
              runs=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$HEAD_SHA/check-runs?per_page=100" \
                --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "SonarCloud Analysis")]' \
                2>/dev/null || echo 'null')
              active=$(printf '%s' "$runs" \
                | jq '[.[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length' \
                2>/dev/null || echo 1)
              producer=$(printf '%s' "$runs" \
                | jq -r 'map(select(.status == "completed"))
                         | sort_by(.started_at) | last
                         | .conclusion // empty' \
                2>/dev/null || true)
              if [ "$active" = "0" ] && [ -n "$producer" ] && [ "$producer" != "success" ]; then
                echo "❌ The SonarCloud Analysis job concluded '$producer', so no analysis of $HEAD_SHA is coming."
                echo "Fix or re-run SonarCloud Analysis, then re-run this job."
                exit 1
              fi
              if [ "$active" != "0" ]; then
                held=$(( $(date +%s) + publish_window ))
                if [ "$held" -gt "$deadline" ]; then deadline=$held; fi
              fi
              echo "No SonarCloud analysis of $HEAD_SHA yet (last analyzed: ${analyzed:-none}), waiting ..."
            fi
            if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
              echo "❌ No SonarCloud analysis of $HEAD_SHA appeared within $(( publish_window / 60 )) min of SonarCloud Analysis finishing (or 60 min with no such job)."
              echo "Check the SonarCloud Analysis job, then re-run this job."
              exit 1
            fi
            sleep 60
          done

  all-checks-pass:
    name: All Checks Pass
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    needs:
      [
        lint,
        typecheck,
        test-unit,
        test-unit-base,
        test-integration,
        binary-smoke,
        wheel-fresh-resolution,
        go-frontend,
        toolchain-tests,
        reference-graphs,
        rust-graph-core,
        sonar-gate,
        greptile-gate,
      ]
    timeout-minutes: 5

    steps:
      - name: Check all jobs
        run: |
          echo "Lint: ${{ needs.lint.result }}"
          echo "Typecheck: ${{ needs.typecheck.result }}"
          echo "Unit Tests: ${{ needs.test-unit.result }}"
          echo "Integration Tests: ${{ needs.test-integration.result }}"
          echo "Binary Smoke: ${{ needs.binary-smoke.result }}"
          echo "Wheel Smoke: ${{ needs.wheel-fresh-resolution.result }}"
          echo "Go Frontend: ${{ needs.go-frontend.result }}"
          echo "Toolchain Tests: ${{ needs.toolchain-tests.result }}"
          echo "Reference Graphs: ${{ needs.reference-graphs.result }}"
          echo "Rust Graph Core: ${{ needs.rust-graph-core.result }}"

          if [[ "${{ needs.lint.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Lint failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.typecheck.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Type check failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.test-unit.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Unit tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.test-unit-base.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Base-install unit tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.test-integration.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Integration tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.binary-smoke.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Binary smoke test failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.wheel-fresh-resolution.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Wheel smoke test (unlocked resolution) failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.go-frontend.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Go frontend job failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.toolchain-tests.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Toolchain tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.reference-graphs.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Reference graphs differ: see the job's log"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.rust-graph-core.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Rust graph core job failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Same skip semantics: the gate is skipped on non-PR events and on
          # PRs SonarCloud never analyzes (Dependabot, forks, non-main base);
          # wherever it does run, anything but success blocks the merge.
          if [[ "${{ needs.sonar-gate.result }}" != "success" \
             && "${{ needs.sonar-gate.result }}" != "skipped" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Sonar gate failed: zero open SonarCloud issues on the head commit are required"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Skipped only outside a pull request (a push to main, a dispatch);
          # on every pull request anything but success blocks the merge.
          if [[ "${{ needs.greptile-gate.result }}" != "success" \
             && "${{ needs.greptile-gate.result }}" != "skipped" ]]; then
            echo "❌ Greptile gate failed: Greptile scored the head commit below 5/5"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ All checks passed!"

FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.8@sha256:5cc1805e2426484abca4ad46ea783bab281fdb225fd82d8ce6d66a81254bac85 AS uv

# The crate the project depends on, cgr-graph-rs, is built from rust/ during
# uv sync. Debian's cargo trails its locked dependencies (trixie ships rustc
# 1.85; tree-sitter-language needs 1.90), so the toolchain comes from here,
# no older than RUST_TOOLCHAIN in .clusterfuzzlite/Dockerfile, which the fuzz
# build proves the crate with on every pull request.
FROM rust:1.100.0-slim-trixie@sha256:e9d95b74296f7126a83ae3d041aeaba1ff4c478f13abc5cc034fcf7c131c3d4a AS rust

FROM python:3.15-slim@sha256:65a65fc7b30b06cb6df4930fd4650697cb23f4c2698ab81fc87e4b031bc36928 AS builder

COPY --from=uv /uv /uvx /bin/
COPY --chmod=755 scripts/distrust_ca_roots.sh /usr/local/sbin/

# Naming ca-certificates upgrades it to the archive's current release: the
# pinned base is a snapshot whose CA store can predate a root's removal, as
# with emSign ECC Root CA - G3 in October 2026. The eMudhra roots the archive
# still ships are then deselected. cargo fetches through this store.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates cmake build-essential git libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libzstd-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && \
    distrust_ca_roots.sh

COPY --from=rust /usr/local/rustup /usr/local/rustup
COPY --from=rust /usr/local/cargo /usr/local/cargo
ENV RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH

WORKDIR /app

# uv installs its managed Python interpreter outside the project directory by
# default ($HOME/.local/share/uv/python, i.e. /root/.local when run as root).
# .venv only symlinks to that interpreter, so pin the install dir under /app
# and copy it into the final stage too, or the venv's python symlink dangles
# once /root is left behind.
#
# uv only populates this directory when it actually downloads a managed
# interpreter -- if the pinned Python version ever matched this image's
# system Python, uv would use that instead and never create the
# directory, and the unconditional COPY below would fail the build
# outright. only-managed rules that out: uv always uses (and downloads
# if needed) its own interpreter, never the system one.
ENV UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/app/.uv-python
ENV UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed

# .python-version must arrive with the manifests: without it this first sync
# falls back to the newest managed Python allowed by requires-python (which
# moves with each uv release), and the later sync, once COPY . . brings in the
# pin, rebuilds .venv on the pinned version. --no-install-local leaves out
# the project and cgr-graph-rs, a path dependency built from rust/ (with the
# cargo above), as neither source is here until COPY . . brings it.
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --extra treesitter-full --extra memgraph --no-install-local --no-binary-package pymgclient

COPY . .
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --extra treesitter-full --extra memgraph --no-binary-package pymgclient

FROM python:3.15-slim@sha256:65a65fc7b30b06cb6df4930fd4650697cb23f4c2698ab81fc87e4b031bc36928

COPY --chmod=755 scripts/distrust_ca_roots.sh /usr/local/sbin/

# The CA store as in the builder: the LLM clients verify TLS against it
# through httpx2's truststore context, not certifi.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates ripgrep libssl3 zlib1g libzstd1 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && \
    distrust_ca_roots.sh

RUN useradd --create-home appuser
USER appuser
WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app/.uv-python /app/.uv-python
COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app/.venv /app/.venv
COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app/codebase_rag /app/codebase_rag
COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app/codec /app/codec
COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app/cgr /app/cgr
COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app/pyproject.toml /app/pyproject.toml

ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

COPY --chmod=755 <<'EOF' /app/entrypoint.sh
#!/bin/sh
ARCH=$(uname -m)
case "$ARCH" in
    x86_64)  LIBDIR="/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu" ;;
    aarch64) LIBDIR="/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu" ;;
    *)       LIBDIR="/lib" ;;
esac
export LD_PRELOAD="$LIBDIR/libz.so.1:$LIBDIR/libzstd.so.1"
exec code-graph-rag "$@"
EOF

ENTRYPOINT ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]
CMD ["mcp-server"]

sampled_files.README.md:
# Code-Graph-RAG Code-Graph-RAG parses a multi-language codebase with Tree-sitter, sharpened by compiler-grade frontends and runtime traces where available, builds a knowledge graph of its structure in an embedded graph database that needs no server, and lets you query, edit, and optimise that code in plain English. It works across a monorepo of mixed languages under one unified graph schema.

1. Index: cgr start --update-graph parses a repository into a knowledge graph (sped up)

2. Ask: cgr start answers questions and edits code, grounded in that graph

## Latest News 🔥 - **Security Fix**: Addressed a potential issue with parameter defaults. - **Stack Handling**: Improved stack management for Qdrant and Memgraph. See [NEWS.md](NEWS.md) for the full history. ## What It Does Point Code-Graph-RAG at a repository and it reads every source file, extracts functions, classes, methods, modules, and the relationships between them, and stores the result as an interconnected graph. Once the graph exists you can: - Ask questions about the codebase in natural language and get answers grounded in the real structure. - Retrieve the actual source of any function, class, or method by name or by intent. - Edit code through the agent with AST-based surgical patching and a diff preview before anything changes. - Optimise code against language best practices or your own coding standards. - Find dead code by walking call and reference edges from entry points. - Search and rewrite structurally by AST pattern with ast-grep. - Overlay runtime behaviour: trace a test run (or pull production eBPF profiles) with `cgr trace` and merge the calls that actually happened into the graph, exposing dispatch that static analysis cannot see. ## How It Works The system has two components: 1. **Multi-language parser.** A Tree-sitter based parser reads the codebase and ingests functions, classes, methods, modules, and their relationships into the graph under a single language-agnostic schema. Where a toolchain is available, compiler-grade frontends layer exact facts on top (libclang for C/C++, `go/types` for Go, and opt-in Roslyn, `javac` and Jedi for C#, Java and Python), and [dynamic tracing](docs/guide/dynamic-tracing.md) merges calls observed at runtime. Tree-sitter stays the backbone: a trace only sees code that ran, and a compiler frontend only covers what its toolchain can build. 2. **RAG system** (`codebase_rag/`). An interactive CLI that turns natural language into Cypher queries, retrieves matching code, and drives AI-powered editing and optimisation. ``` Source Code -> Tree-sitter Parser -> AST Analysis -> Knowledge Graph | User Query -> AI Model (Cypher Gen) -> Cypher Query -> Graph Results -> Response ``` The graph is stored in an embedded SQLite file by default. Memgraph and Neo4j are opt-in backends that run the same Cypher; [Graph Backends](docs/architecture/embedded-graph.md) compares them. See the [Architecture Overview](docs/architecture/overview.md) and [Graph Schema](docs/architecture/graph-schema.md) for the full picture. ## Supported Languages Python, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, Rust, Go, Java, C, C++, C#, PHP, Lua, Dart, and Julia are fully supported. Scala is in development, and Ruby, Kotlin, Swift, Elixir, Haskell, Solidity, Bash, and Nix have structural support (modules, functions, classes where the language has them, and imports) through the pluggable ast-grep tier. See the [Language Support](docs/architecture/language-support.md) matrix for per-language capabilities. ## Installation `cgr` is published to PyPI. Install it system-wide with the `treesitter-full` (tree-sitter grammars), `ast-grep` (Ruby, Kotlin, Swift, Elixir, Haskell, Solidity, Bash, Nix) and `semantic` (vector search) extras: ```bash # with uv (recommended) uv tool install "code-graph-rag[treesitter-full,ast-grep,semantic]" # or with pipx pipx install "code-graph-rag[treesitter-full,ast-grep,semantic]" ``` ### Which version am I getting? Three version lines exist and they intentionally differ: | where | what it tracks | |---|---| | git tags | every version, one per merge | | GitHub Releases (binaries, signatures) | every 50th version, plus any security fix, breaking change or merge labelled `release now` | | PyPI | every 50th version, plus any security fix, breaking change or merge labelled `release now` | So the newest tag on `main` usually runs ahead of the newest release, often by tens of patch versions; they coincide only just after a release. Nothing is stuck, the cadences differ by design. A security fix, a breaking change or a merge a maintainer labels `release now` does NOT wait for the cadence: each ships a release and a PyPI upload immediately. `uv tool install` and `pipx install` give you the newest PyPI version, which is the newest RELEASE, not the newest tag. Interim tags exist so every merge is addressable; binaries and PyPI uploads follow the cadence above. To run code newer than the latest release, install from git: ```bash uv tool install "code-graph-rag[treesitter-full,ast-grep,semantic] @ git+https://github.com/vitali87/code-graph-rag@main" ``` To upgrade an existing install, run `uv tool upgrade code-graph-rag` (with pipx, `pipx upgrade code-graph-rag`, or `pipx reinstall code-graph-rag` for a git install). [Upgrade](docs/getting-started/installation.md#upgrade) covers the other install methods. You also need Python 3.12+ and `ripgrep`. The graph lives in an embedded SQLite file by default, so there is no database server to run: no Docker and no `cmake`. Memgraph and Neo4j remain available as opt-in backends ([Graph Backends](docs/architecture/embedded-graph.md)). Full prerequisites, source installs, and environment setup are in the [Installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md) guide. > [!NOTE] > cgr requires its native extension, `cgr-graph-rs`, which ships for CPython 3.12 or newer on Linux (x86_64, aarch64), macOS and Windows x64, so it installs on those platforms only. Older system interpreters (Debian Bookworm ships 3.11) need the interpreter pinned explicitly; see [Installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md#older-system-interpreters) for the commands. ## Quick Start ```bash # Parse a repository into the graph, then query it cgr start --repo-path /path/to/repo --update-graph cgr start --repo-path /path/to/repo ``` The graph is written to `~/.cgr/graph.sqlite` (set `SQLITE_GRAPH_PATH` to move it). To use Memgraph instead, install the driver with the `memgraph` extra, set `GRAPH_BACKEND=memgraph`, and start the packaged Memgraph + Qdrant stack with `cgr daemon up`. Repeat the first command for each repository you want indexed; the graph is shared, and syncing one project leaves the others alone. To start over from an empty graph, add `--clean` — it deletes **every** project in the shared graph, not just this one, and asks for confirmation first when other projects would be destroyed. A default index leaves out the opt-in [capture groups](docs/architecture/graph-schema.md#capture-groups); add them with `--capture` or `CGR_CAPTURE`. The [Quick Start](docs/getting-started/quickstart.md) guide walks through parsing, querying, and exporting in five minutes. ## MCP Server Code-Graph-RAG runs as an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server so Claude Code and other MCP clients can query and edit your codebase directly. See the [MCP Server](docs/guide/mcp-server.md) guide for setup. ## Documentation **Getting Started** - [Installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md) - [Quick Start](docs/getting-started/quickstart.md) - [Configuration](docs/getting-started/configuration.md) **User Guide** - [CLI Reference](docs/guide/cli-reference.md) - [Interactive Querying](docs/guide/interactive-querying.md) - [Code Optimisation](docs/guide/code-optimization.md) - [Dead Code Detection](docs/guide/dead-code.md) - [Dynamic Call Tracing](docs/guide/dynamic-tracing.md) - [Graph Export](docs/guide/graph-export.md) - [Real-Time Updates](docs/guide/realtime-updates.md) - [C/C++ Semantic Mode](docs/guide/cpp-semantic-mode.md) - [MCP Server](docs/guide/mcp-server.md) - [Porting Between Languages](docs/guide/porting.md) **Architecture** - [Overview](docs/architecture/overview.md) - [Graph Schema](docs/architecture/graph-schema.md) - [Graph Backends](docs/architecture/embedded-graph.md) - [Language Support](docs/architecture/language-support.md) - [Data-Flow Edges](docs/architecture/data-flow-edges.md) **Python SDK** - [Overview](docs/sdk/overview.md) - [Graph Loader](docs/sdk/graph-loader.md) - [Cypher Generator](docs/sdk/cypher-generator.md) - [Semantic Search](docs/sdk/semantic-search.md) **Advanced** - [Adding Languages](docs/advanced/adding-languages.md) - [Ignore Patterns](docs/advanced/ignore-patterns.md) - [Building Binaries](docs/advanced/building-binaries.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/advanced/troubleshooting.md) ## Enterprise Services Code-Graph-RAG is open source and free to use. For organisations that need more, we offer **fully managed cloud-hosted solutions** and **on-premise deployments**: - **Cloud-Hosted Deployment**: Managed cloud infrastructure for both the graph database and the AI agent connection. Zero infrastructure overhead, so we handle scaling, updates, and availability while your team focuses on building. - **On-Premise & Air-Gapped Deployment**: Deploy Code-Graph-RAG entirely within your own environment, including air-gapped networks. Full data sovereignty for regulated industries and security-sensitive organisations. We also offer custom development, integration consulting, technical support contracts, and team training. **[View plans & pricing at code-graph-rag.com](https://code-graph-rag.com/enterprise)** ## Contributing Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for contribution guidelines. Good first PRs come from the TODO issues. ## Support For issues or questions, check the [Troubleshooting](docs/advanced/troubleshooting.md) guide first, then open an issue. If cgr is useful to you, please consider pledging support on [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/vitali87). cgr links the page under `cgr --version` and, in a terminal, after most commands finish; set `CGR_SPONSOR_PLEDGE=false` to hide that line. ## Accessibility [ACCESSIBILITY.md](ACCESSIBILITY.md) describes what cgr and its documentation support for people using assistive technology or alternative settings, the known limitations and their workarounds, and how to report a barrier. ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party components and their licences are credited on the [Credits page](https://docs.code-graph-rag.com/credits/).

    "pygments>=2.20.0",
    # Imported directly (embedder, health checks, token counting, web
    # search). It used to arrive only through the provider SDKs, and
    # google-genai 3 moved to httpx2, which a fresh install then took alone.
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    # certifi is the CA bundle httpx and requests verify against; 2026.10.23
    # is the first without the distrusted eMudhra roots. Declared so an
    # upgrade over an older install moves it too.
    "certifi>=2026.10.23",
    # The embedded graph's `=~`: unlike `re`, a match takes a timeout, so a
    # backtracking pattern stops at the query's deadline. tiktoken already
    # installs it.
    "regex>=2024.11.6",
    # The Rust half that does the work behind the Python interface
    # (rust/cgr_graph_rs), required everywhere: cgr does not run without it.
    # It ships as abi3 wheels for CPython on Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS and
    # Windows x64, and has no sdist, so other platforms cannot install cgr.
    # The floor is the crate version this code was written against, raised
    # with each crate release.
    "cgr-graph-rs>=0.1.8,<0.2",
]

[project.scripts]
code-graph-rag = "codebase_rag.cli:app"
cgr = "codebase_rag.cli:app"

[project.entry-points.pytest11]
cgr_trace = "codebase_rag.trace.pytest_plugin"

[tool.uv]
package = true

# Patched grammars: upstream tree-sitter-c drops declarations after a
# #define whose value embeds a block comment (issue #555). Our forks carry
# the repeat(preproc_arg) fix; drop these overrides once upstream releases it.
[tool.uv.sources]
# A checkout builds the crate it carries (with a Rust toolchain), so the
# Python and Rust halves of a change are tested together; installs from
# PyPI get the published wheels.
cgr-graph-rs = { path = "rust/cgr_graph_rs" }
tree-sitter-c = { git = "https://github.com/vitali87/tree-sitter-c", rev = "fa327ad98f847f8173fc46926be4165c7971f960" }
tree-sitter-cpp = { git = "https://github.com/vitali87/tree-sitter-cpp", rev = "b4a7be2f62f36dd460a14b2d1728d42d81d2c486" }

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["codebase_rag*", "codec*", "cgr*"]
exclude = ["*.tests", "*.tests.*"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
codebase_rag = [
    "docker-compose.yaml",
    "parsers/csharp_frontend/roslyn/*.cs",
    "parsers/csharp_frontend/roslyn/*.csproj",
    "parsers/go_frontend/gotypes/*.go",
    "parsers/go_frontend/gotypes/go.mod",
    "parsers/go_frontend/gotypes/go.sum",
    "parsers/java_frontend/javac/cgr/*.java",
    "parsers/ast_grep_patterns/*.yaml",
    "analyzers/ast_grep_rules/*/*.yaml",
    # Julia's pip grammar ships no HIGHLIGHTS_QUERY, so its highlights come
    # only from this fallback file; without it the wheel silently disables
    # Julia modifier/decorator extraction (issue #1882 review).
    "queries/highlights/*.scm",
    # The tracer agents the dynamic-tracing guide builds or loads; `cgr trace
    # agent <language>` prints where an installed copy keeps each (issue #2684).
    "trace/c_agent/*.c",
    "trace/lua_agent/*.lua",
    "trace/dart_collector/pubspec.yaml",
    "trace/dart_collector/pubspec.lock",
    "trace/dart_collector/bin/*.dart",
    "trace/jvm_agent/MANIFEST.MF",
    "trace/jvm_agent/src/cgr/trace/*.java",
]
# The provenance manifest hashes this file to stamp each index with its codec
# schema; without it every installed build writes a null hash and
# `cgr diff-index` refuses its indexes (issue #2399).
codec = ["schema.proto"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = [
    "jedi>=0.19",
    "pytest>=8.4.1",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "testcontainers>=4.9.0",
    "libclang>=18.1.1",
    "filelock>=3.12",
    "ast-grep-py>=0.51.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    # The suite exercises the Memgraph backend with a mocked server, but
    # imports the real driver's exception types to do it.
    "pymgclient>=1.6.0",
    # The `sqlite` vector store's tests run against a real sqlite-vec file.
    "sqlite-vec>=0.1.9",
]

cpp = [
    "libclang>=18.1.1",
]

# Memgraph is an optional backend since the embedded graph became the
# default (issue #386). Its driver is a C extension that builds with cmake
# wherever no wheel fits, the setup step first-time users tripped on.
# TransientError, which the ingestor retries, first appears in 1.6.0.
memgraph = [
    "pymgclient>=1.6.0",
]

# Neo4j is an optional backend (issue #1590), so a default install must not
# pay for a driver it will never load.
neo4j = [
    "neo4j>=5.28.1",
]

treesitter-full = [
    "tree-sitter-python>=0.23.6",
    "tree-sitter-javascript>=0.23.1",
    "tree-sitter-typescript>=0.23.2",
    "tree-sitter-rust>=0.24.0",
    "tree-sitter-go>=0.23.4",
    "tree-sitter-scala>=0.24.0",
    "tree-sitter-java>=0.23.5",
    "tree-sitter-c>=0.24.1",
    "tree-sitter-cpp>=0.23.0",
    "tree-sitter-lua>=0.0.19",
    "tree-sitter-julia>=0.23.1",
    "tree-sitter-php>=0.24.1",
    "tree-sitter-c-sharp>=0.23.5",
    # Exact pin: PyPI's tree-sitter-dart is a single-maintainer repackaging of
    # a fork, so a new release is a new publisher decision, not a grammar fix.
    "tree-sitter-dart==0.1.0",
    "tree-sitter-sql>=0.3.11",
    "tree-sitter-markdown>=0.5.1",
]

# sqlite-vec is the default vector store's, on the platforms it ships wheels
# for (it has no sdist), which cover every one torch ships wheels for; no
# marker tells musl from glibc, and torch has no musl wheels either.
# qdrant-client is for CGR_VECTOR_STORE_BACKEND=qdrant, the default before it.
semantic = [
    "qdrant-client>=1.9.0",
    # The gRPC client verifies TLS against grpcio's own roots.pem; 1.84.1 is
    # the first without emSign ECC Root CA - G3.
    "grpcio>=1.84.1",
    "sqlite-vec>=0.1.9; (sys_platform == 'linux' and (platform_machine == 'x86_64' or platform_machine == 'aarch64')) or sys_platform == 'darwin' or (sys_platform == 'win32' and platform_machine == 'AMD64')",
    "torch>=2.6.0",
    "transformers>=5.0.0",
    # transformers downloads the UniXcoder model through it, and nothing
    # outside this extra imports it, so a default install leaves it out with
    # the five packages it brings (hf-xet, fsspec, tqdm, filelock, packaging).
    "huggingface-hub[hf-xet]>=1.7.2",
]

milvus = [
    "pymilvus[milvus-lite]>=3.0.0",
    # As in `semantic`: pymilvus's gRPC client trusts grpcio's roots.pem.
    "grpcio>=1.84.1",
]

# The default `sqlite` vector store alone, for an install that computes its
# embeddings elsewhere (CGR_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai): vectors in a file
# beside the embedded graph, so semantic search needs no server either.
sqlite-vec = [
    "sqlite-vec>=0.1.9",
]

ast-grep = [
    "ast-grep-py>=0.51.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
]
python-semantics = [
    "jedi>=0.19",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py312"
exclude = ["codec/", "benchmarks/", "optimize/"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "UP", "PL", "T201", "S"]
ignore = [
    "E501",     # line too long
    "PLR2004",  # magic value comparison (too noisy)
    "PLC0415",  # import not at top-level (intentional lazy imports)
    "PLR0913",  # too many arguments (often unavoidable)
    "PLR0917",  # too many positional arguments (often unavoidable)
    "PLR0911",  # too many return statements
    "PLR0912",  # too many branches
    "PLR0915",  # too many statements
    "PLW2901",  # loop variable overwritten (intentional for .strip())
    "PLW0603",  # global statement (singleton pattern)
    "S101",     # assert (Bandit skips B101 too)
    "S105",     # password-by-name heuristic: fires on *_TOKEN / PASS_* constants; secret scanning covers real secrets
    "S106",     # same heuristic for keyword arguments
    "S107",     # same heuristic for argument defaults
    "S603",     # any subprocess call with an argv list; the shell=True rules (S602, S604, S605) stay on
    "S607",     # toolchains resolve from PATH by design; shutil.which reads the same PATH
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests are outside Bandit's and SonarCloud's security scope too.
"**/tests/**" = ["T201", "S"]
"benchmarks/**" = ["T201"]
"evals/flows_corpus/**" = ["T201"]
# The corpus builder is a CLI script; its output is the point.
"fuzz/build_corpus.py" = ["T201"]
# The embedded graph engine compiles Cypher to SQL, so composing SQL text is
# its job. Identifiers in that text are generated by the compiler and string
# literals pass through `sql_str`; every value supplied with a query reaches
# SQLite as a bound parameter, never spliced into the statement.
"codebase_rag/embedded_graph/**" = ["S608"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"

[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.12"

[tool.ty.src]
exclude = ["codebase_rag/tests/test_cypher_queries.py", "codebase_rag/tests/test_code_retrieval.py", "codebase_rag/tests/test_call_resolver.py", "benchmarks/", "optimize/"]

[tool.coverage.run]
# `codebase_rag/constants/` is excluded because coverage cannot say anything
# useful about it, not because it is untested (issue #1599).
#
# Those 31 modules are almost entirely module-level assignments. A constant
# definition executes exactly once, at import, and cannot fail to execute if
# the module is imported at all -- so the measurement is 100% or 0% depending
# on whether tracing had started by then, never on whether anything is tested.
# Measured under pytest it is 0/2858 lines, because conftest imports
# `graph_updater` (which alone pulls all 31) during collection, before
# pytest-cov begins tracing. Importing the same package after starting
# coverage manually records the lines normally.
#
# Keeping it in the denominator understated source coverage by ~2856 lines and
# made `constants/` read as the largest gap in the tree while carrying no
# signal in either direction. Excluding it makes the remaining figure mean
# something; it does not hide dead code, since an unused constant executes at
# import exactly like a used one and coverage could never have flagged it.
#
# This is not a new judgement: `sonar-project.properties` already carries
# `sonar.coverage.exclusions=...,codebase_rag/constants/**`. The two tools
# disagreed, and this makes Codecov match the call the project had made.
omit = ["codebase_rag/constants/*"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# loadgroup honors the xdist_group marker that pins the integration dir to
# one worker; for unmarked tests it schedules identically to the default.
# xdist workers decide their grouping flag from the parsed args/ini before
# any conftest hook fires (xdist remote.py setup_config), so this must be
# an ini-level option; every dependency set that carries pytest also
# carries pytest-xdist, so the flag always parses. The shard plugin
# registers `--shard`, which CI uses to split the suite across jobs
# (codebase_rag/tests/suite_shards.py says why it is not a conftest hook).
addopts = "--dist=loadgroup -p codebase_rag.tests.suite_shards"
testpaths = ["codebase_rag/tests"]
norecursedirs = ["grammars", ".git", "__pycache__", "*.egg-info", ".venv", "venv"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (may download models or require external services)",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests requiring Docker",
    "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "bandit>=1.9.2",
    "coverage>=7.13.0",
    "pre-commit>=4.2.0",
    "pyinstaller>=6.14.1",
    "pytest>=9.0.2",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    # ty resolves the Memgraph driver's types where the code names them.
    "pymgclient>=1.6.0",
    "ruff>=0.5.5",
    "ty>=0.0.7",
    "types-protobuf>=5.0.0",
]
docs = [
    # Exact pin while Zensical is pre-1.0.
    "zensical==0.1.1",
]
fuzz = [
    "atheris>=2.3.0",
]
# Builds the cgr-graph-rs wheels (.github/workflows/rust-wheels.yml): zig
# links each Linux wheel against the oldest glibc or musl its tag promises.
rust-wheels = [
    "maturin==1.16.0",
    # Only the Linux wheels are linked with zig, and it ships no Windows build.
    "ziglang==0.17.1; sys_platform == 'linux'",
]

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["codebase_rag/tests", "scripts", "benchmarks", "optimize"]
skips = ["B101"]

# Phistory

[中文](README_zh.md)

Phistory tracks how system prompts change across popular coding-agent CLIs like Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness, Antigravity, Grok Build, Kimi Code, MiMo Code, OpenClaw, Hermes, Kimi CLI, opencode, Pi, and Oh My Pi.

Open the web viewer to compare prompt snapshots across versions and see how agent design changes through prompts, tools, policies, and runtime instructions.

**Start here:** [phistory.cc](https://phistory.cc/)

> Checks for new releases hourly. Archive last updated: **2026-11-21 00:56 UTC**.

![Phistory prompt diff viewer](docs/screenshot.png)

## Why Use It

- Follow how Anthropic, OpenAI, and other agent builders iterate on system prompts over time.
- See when new tools, permission checks, model defaults, and user-confirmation rules are added.
- Compare how different CLIs structure agent behavior, tool use, and developer-facing constraints.
- Cite stable prompt snapshots in posts, research notes, audits, or debugging reports.

## How It Works

For each supported release, Phistory installs the exact CLI package and runs each configured snapshot through [`claude-tap`](https://github.com/WEIFENG2333/claude-tap), captures the prompt-bearing HTTP request without calling the real model provider, and stores the result under `captures/<agent>/<version>/variants/<variant>/` with `prompt.md`, `trace.jsonl`, and `meta.json`. The `default` snapshot runs each CLI the way its users do, through a real terminal when it ships one; selected models or alternative surfaces are stored as additional variants. `prompt.md` is rendered from the archived trace, so every block of the request survives into it: each system block and its cache boundary, reminder blocks, and system messages interleaved with the conversation.

GitHub Actions checks automatically tracked CLI releases every hour and commits new snapshots when they appear.

The viewer supports Chinese translations for runtime prompt diffs and readable trace fields. Unchanged paragraphs reuse shared translations across versions; original evidence is preserved. See [translation setup and storage](docs/translations.md) and [model evaluation](docs/translation-evaluation.md).

## Local Development

Use the hosted viewer at [phistory.cc](https://phistory.cc/). These commands are for local development, capture reproduction, historical backfills, and regenerating generated files.

```bash
# Install the locked development environment.
uv sync --all-groups

# Capture the latest release and every configured snapshot for each CLI.
uv run phistory capture --latest --agents claude-code,codex,dsh,antigravity,grok,kimi-code,mimo,openclaw,hermes,kimi,opencode,pi,omp

# Capture only selected Codex snapshots.
uv run phistory capture --latest --agents codex --variants default,gpt-5.5,gpt-5.6

# Capture a historical version range for one agent.
uv run phistory backfill claude-code --from 2.1.113 --to latest

# Translate archived prose using credentials configured outside the repository.
uv run phistory translate --all-captured

# Regenerate README.md, README_zh.md, docs/captures.md, captures/index.json, and llms.txt.
uv run phistory render-index

# Build the complete static site, including Chinese translation indexes.
uv run phistory build-site
python -m http.server --directory .phistory-cache/site
```

## Supported Agents

- Claude Code (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code`)
- Codex CLI (`@openai/codex`)
- DeepSeek Harness (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`)
- Antigravity CLI (`google-antigravity/antigravity-cli`)
- Grok Build (`@xai-official/grok`)
- Kimi Code (`@moonshot-ai/kimi-code`)
- MiMo Code (`@mimo-ai/cli`)
- OpenClaw (`openclaw`)
- Hermes Agent (`hermes-agent`)
- Kimi CLI (`MoonshotAI/kimi-cli`)
- opencode (`opencode-ai`)
- Pi (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)
- Oh My Pi (`@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`)

repository.readme:
[English](README.md) | [한국어](README.ko.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

Understand your system as AI agents change its code.

A map of what your code does and why, kept as Markdown in your repository
and read by both you and your coding agent.

Download · Try it in the browser · Guide

![A five-second loop of the Atlas map: a capability under Code evidence is selected, the lines to what it depends on and what uses it light up, and a panel opens naming them](docs/assets/readme/map-select.gif) ## Why Coding agents now change code faster than a team can keep a picture of it in their heads. Atlas keeps that picture beside the code: what each part is for, which files implement it, what depends on what, and what nobody knows yet. Your agent reads it before a task and proposes updates after; you keep, correct or reject each change as a Markdown diff. - **Your agent starts with context.** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Antigravity read the concepts, code paths, dependencies and open questions a task touches, over MCP. - **You own the record.** One Markdown file per concept in an `atlas/` folder, versioned and reviewed in Git like the code. - **You decide what is true.** Every agent edit is a Markdown diff you keep, correct or revert; in the app's own chat each write waits for you. - **It says what it does not know.** A line on the map is a declared relationship, not proof of runtime impact; missing evidence shows as unknown, never as safe. How is this different from a code graph, a wiki, Obsidian or `CLAUDE.md`? See [Atlas compared](docs/guide/atlas-compared.md), which also says when those are the better choice. ## Quick start 1. **Install** the app from the [download page](https://ontologyatlas.com/en/download/), or open the [browser version](https://ontologyatlas.com/en/topology/). 2. **Open a folder.** Atlas reads its Markdown in place, or starts an `atlas/` folder in your repository, and shows the path before it writes anything. 3. **Connect your agent.** In **Agents › MCP**, press **Connect** for your tool, restart the agent, and ask about your next task. macOS (Apple Silicon) is signed and notarized and carries the MCP server inside the app. Windows x64 is an unsigned beta. On Linux, use the browser version or run the [CLI and MCP server from a source checkout](cli/README.md#set-up-from-a-source-checkout). [Releases](https://github.com/wlsdks/ontology-atlas/releases) list each version's files and checksums. ## See it ![The Atlas map of this repository's own ontology with the MCP tool server capability selected: lit lines run to the nine concepts it depends on and the two that use it, across the domains, and a panel on the right lists them](docs/assets/readme/topology-overview.png) **Map** — select a concept and the lines to what it depends on and what uses it light up; the panel names each one. Flat, Hex, Domain structure, a 3D tree and Neural are views of the same concepts. [Map](docs/features/map/README.md)

Map · Neural — the same concepts as a volume you can turn; select one to see what it depends on and what uses it.
Projects — what a project is for, how it divides into domains, and what each domain holds.

Library — documents in, cited wiki pages out; find a passage, then check it in the source.
Planning — write plans as Markdown in the open folder's planning/, in the app or the browser; the macOS app can also read another folder in place.

Changes — what was merged in a period, counted and grouped, with the pull requests, commits and files behind it.
Git — each commit by the concepts it changed; an edited document shows up here before you commit it.

Harness — what an agent reads in your repository, what stops it before it acts, and what checks its work.
Automations — scheduled checks, and what each run found.
## How it works ```text your-repo/ ├── src/ └── atlas/ ← cloned, branched and reviewed with the code ├── project.md ├── domains/ capabilities/ elements/ ├── sources/ documents kept exactly as they arrived └── wiki/ pages written from those sources, every fact cited ``` A Markdown file whose frontmatter has `kind:` is one concept: a **project**, a **domain** (a lasting responsibility), a **capability** (something the system does) or an **element** (a part two or more capabilities share). Its `uid` never changes, its `slug` is its current address, and its `path` names the code it describes. This one is abridged from this repository's own map, in [`docs/ontology/`](docs/ontology/capabilities/vault-graph-query.md): ```markdown --- uid: 7c451ebd-9cd0-41a9-bc37-044affac786a slug: capabilities/vault-graph-query kind: capability title: Vault graph query domain: domains/meaning-layer path: mcp/src/tools/graph.mjs dependencies: [elements/graph-compiler, elements/graph-engine, elements/vault-file-store] --- ## Definition Compiles the folder of Markdown files into one typed graph and answers structural questions over it, so a person or agent can ask what a node touches without opening every file. ## Excludes - Writing anything back to the vault. ## Uncertainty - The engine is roughly 6,400 lines and was not read beyond its header. ``` The map, documents, Library and Git screens all read these files, and so does your agent. These MCP tools answer the questions an agent asks most: | Before or after a task, the agent asks | Tool | |---|---| | What is this part for, and what does it exclude? | `get_concept` | | What points at it, before I rename or delete it? | `find_backlinks` | | How are these two concepts connected? | `find_path` | | What may this change affect? | `query_ontology` with `impact` | | Where is this mentioned? | `find_evidence` | | Record what I just built or changed | `add_concepts`, `add_relations`, `patch_concept` | | Is the folder still consistent? | `validate_vault` | Register the server read-only and it offers only the tools that read ([MCP reference](mcp/README.md#read-only-registration-oatlas_read_only)). Your agent reaches the folder two ways: - **MCP:** the agent starts the Atlas MCP server, which reads and writes the folder on disk, even with the app closed. [Connect an agent](docs/guide/connect-agent.md) · [MCP reference](mcp/README.md) - **ACP:** Claude Agent and Codex also run in the app's own chat, where you allow or reject their writes. [Agents](docs/features/agents.md) ## Local-first - No backend, account or telemetry. The folder stays plain Markdown on your disk. - Model calls with your API key or a local model are opt-in, and each records its destination in `.ontology-atlas/llm-audit.jsonl`. - A connected coding agent may send your prompt and what it reads to its own provider; Atlas's log does not cover those transfers. [Trust](docs/guide/trust.md) · [Security](SECURITY.md) ## Limits - **Atlas asks before an agent writes only in the app's chat.** There each file edit and Atlas write waits for you, unless you turn on Auto-approve for that folder; shell commands, deletions and paths outside the folder always ask. An agent connected over MCP writes under its own tool's permission rules. [Agents](docs/features/agents.md) - **Library setup and checks need the app.** In a browser, Library offers the app or adding files. [Library](docs/features/library/workspace.md) - **Changes reads public GitHub pull requests only,** after you ask, and the list may be incomplete; private pull requests are not read. [Change briefing](docs/features/change-briefing.md) - **Git's Pull can change files anywhere in the repository,** not only in the open folder. [Git](docs/features/git.md) ## Status Atlas is early. Our benchmark has not yet shown better answers with Atlas, and Atlas was slower ([the correction](docs/benchmark/README.md#current-measurement-status)). Construction trials, their failures and limits are in [the construction measurements](docs/benchmark/CONSTRUCTION.md). ## Documentation [What is Atlas?](docs/guide/what-is-atlas.md) · [Atlas compared](docs/guide/atlas-compared.md) · [First five minutes](docs/guide/first-five-minutes.md) · [Build the first map from your code](docs/guide/from-your-repo.md) · [What becomes a node?](docs/guide/what-becomes-a-node.md) · [Relations](docs/guide/relations.md) · [Specification](docs/ONTOLOGY-ATLAS-SPEC.md) · [Features](docs/FEATURES.md) · [CLI](cli/README.md) · [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) ## Contributing Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); external pull requests come from forks. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is the contract for people and agents alike. ```bash pnpm install pnpm dev pnpm checks:changed -- --run ``` Installs refuse dependency versions published less than seven days ago; [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md#dependency-installs) explains the install settings and how an urgent security fix skips the wait. [Development checks](docs/DEVELOPMENT-CHECKS.md) covers choosing checks, pre-push and CI, merging, lane budgets, and every repository command. ## Moru Moru is Atlas's pixel seal companion; the compass is the app identity. The repository includes [74 motions, 16 poses and their sources](assets/brand/moru/README.md), with where Moru appears in the app and every drawn motion.

## License [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party notices are in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md), and the full license texts in [public/third-party-licenses.txt](public/third-party-licenses.txt). The pixel mascot and its sources are described in [Brand](docs/design/brand.md).
